warden_holt.name: Warden Holt
warden_holt.title: Warden of the Watch

dialogue.hail: Hail, {name}. Keep your wits about you out here. The [gnolls] have grown bold this season.
dialogue.gnolls: Mangy curs from the camp east of my post. They raid the road and bite anyone who strays from the stones. The watch pays a bounty on [gnoll fangs].
dialogue.gnoll fangs: Bring me four gnoll fangs, pulled from pups or scouts, it matters not. Hand them to me when you have them and I'll pay you from the watch's purse. And if you go near their camp, beware [Grubnak].
dialogue.grubnak: Grubnak the Mangy, their chief. Twice the size of his kin and meaner than a cornered badger. He shows his face at the camp now and then. Don't go alone.
dialogue.tovin: Tovin sent you? That old haggler. If he wants Blackpaw leather, bring me his cord and two Blackpaw pelts. The scouts carry the best of them. I'll cure and stitch the hide myself.

warden_holt.outfitter: Empty-handed, {name}? The wilds took your kit, I'd wager. Here, from the Watch's stores. Try to keep hold of it this time.

hunt_shouts: Not while I hold this post!

dialogue.hail: Move along, {name}. The [Watch] keeps the peace here. If trouble follows you down this road, run to us.
dialogue.watch: We patrol the walls and the road to Greenmoor. Warden Holt keeps a watch house in the far north of Greenmoor, where he can keep an eye on the gnoll camp. If you've a mind for honest work, he pays a bounty on [gnoll fangs].
dialogue.gnoll fangs: Not to me. Take them to Warden Holt. His watch house is past the obelisk, up in the far north of Greenmoor.
dialogue.unknown: I'm on duty, {name}. Ask the Keeper at the hearth if you want stories.

shouts: Stand fast, {name}! The Watch is here!
Not on my road, you mangy cur!
shouts_player: Halt, {name}! In the name of the Watch!

dialogue.hail: Hail, {name}. I walk this road from the Emberhold gate to the [obelisk] and back, sunup to sundown. Slow, aye, but I get there.
dialogue.obelisk: The old stone where the road ends. Past it is gnoll country. Anything with teeth that wanders onto my road gets a sword for its trouble. If you've earned the [Watch]'s trust, I'll come for you when you're in trouble.
dialogue.watch: Friends of the Watch get help on my road. Strangers get a good view. Thin out the gnolls and Warden Holt will see your name goes around.
dialogue.unknown: I'm walking, {name}, not talking. Keep up or step aside.

shouts: Friend of the Watch in trouble!
hunt_shouts: Back to the wilds with you!
shouts_player: Halt, {name}! In the name of the Watch!

dialogue.bind: Hold out your hands to the flame, {name}. There: your soul knows the hearth now. Gate, or your Homeward Stone, will bring you back here.
dialogue.hail: Welcome to Emberhold, {name}. Warm your hands at the [hearth]. It has burned since the [Emberfall], and it will burn long after us. Ask, and I'll [bind] your soul to it, so you always find your way back.
dialogue.hearth: No wood feeds it and no rain drowns it. The Keepers tend it all the same. Those who fall in these lands wake beside a [bindstone], drawn back to warmth.
dialogue.emberfall: The night the sky burned, a star came down into this hollow and would not cool. The first settlers raised walls around its heat. That ember is the one before you.
dialogue.bindstone: The hearth here, and the old obelisk in Greenmoor. When you fall, you wake at the bindstone of the land you fell in. Your belongings, sadly, stay where you dropped.
dialogue.unknown: Many things are forgotten, {name}, but not that one. I don't know it.

dialogue.hail: Welcome, welcome, {name}! Leathers for the road, and I'll take whatever you drag back from it. Fangs, eyes, [whiskers], it's all coin to me. And if you ever want a [proper pack], ask old Tovin.
dialogue.whiskers: Rat whiskers! Brush-makers in the lower city can't get enough. Don't ask me why.
dialogue.unknown: I only know prices, {name}. Ask the Keeper for the rest.
dialogue.proper pack: Not a sack, not some scavenged gnoll bag. A proper pack, the kind I made before my hands got slow. I'm short of cord, though. Rat whiskers twist into cord stronger than wire. Bring me four and we'll begin.

dialogue.hail: Hmph. Iron's good, steel's better, and I've only got iron this season. The [gnolls] keep hitting the ore carts.
dialogue.gnolls: Take your complaint to Warden Holt, not me. Or take a sword to them. I'll sell you one.

dialogue.hail: The Hearthbank of Emberhold, at your service, {name}. What you leave with me stays safe when you [fall].
dialogue.fall: Fall in the wilds and what you carry stays on your corpse. What's in my vault stays in my vault. Choose wisely what you carry.
dialogue.unknown: I'm afraid I only keep accounts, {name}.

dialogue.hail: Shh! Easy, {name}, you'll spook the [trout]. Name's Merrick. I sell poles and bait to anyone with the patience to use them.
dialogue.trout: Greenmoor trout, fat as your fist. Most of them, anyway. There's one in this pond a good deal bigger. [Old Gulper], I call him.
dialogue.old gulper: Thirty years I've been after that fish. He's snapped more of my lines than I can count. One of these days, {name}. One of these days.
dialogue.unknown: Hm? Sorry, I was watching my line.

merricks_line_word.hail: There you are, {name}! Beat you here. Look at it: clear to the bottom. Now, that vial of yours.
merricks_line_word.unknown: Later, {name}. Let's see that vial first.

merricks_line_pond.hail: {name}! Come to watch the water run clear? The fish are biting again, thanks to you and Corran. Poles and bait, same as ever. Mind you don't spook the [trout].
merricks_line_pond.trout: Greenmoor trout, fat as your fist, and hungry again. There's one in this pond a good deal bigger, mind. [Old Gulper], I call him.
merricks_line_pond.old gulper: Thirty years I've been after that fish. He's snapped more of my lines than I can count. Now that the water's sweet again, he'll be back. One of these days, {name}. One of these days.
merricks_line_pond.unknown: Hm? Sorry, {name}, I was watching my line. Old habits.

dialogue.hail: Hmph. What. Fish ain't biting. Water's gone sour. I could try silk, but I fear it's way too far away, and it'll still rot in this sour water. What I need is the [sinew] from the rats.
dialogue.sinew: Yes, the sinew. The rats are drinking from the same streams. Their sinew's already steeped in whatever's wrong. Five lengths of sinew, {name}. That's enough to twist a line that'll hold.
dialogue.unknown: Did I ask? Rat sinew, {name}. Five lengths. Else leave me to my ale.

merricks_line_sinew.hail: Well? What are you waiting for, {name}? The cave under the first hills, west of the pond. [Corran]'s waiting at the mouth. Something's fouling the [spring].
merricks_line_sinew.corran: Watchman Corran. Good man, bad jokes. He'll go down with you. Keep him standing and he'll keep you standing.
merricks_line_sinew.spring: Whole zone drinks from it. Go look, you and Corran. Don't drink what's down there. Bring me word of what's rotting the water, or kill it, if it has a throat.
merricks_line_sinew.sinew: Already twisting it. Won't matter a lick while the water's sour, though. The [spring], {name}.

merricks_line_spring.hail: You're back! And? What was down there, {name}? Tell me about the [blightmother].
merricks_line_spring.blightmother: The what? A spider? Show me. Put it in my hand. I'll not believe it till I've seen it.
merricks_line_spring.spring: Clean, you say? At the source? Show me what was fouling it first.

watchman_corran.name: Watchman Corran
watchman_corran.title: Emberhold Watch

dialogue.hail: Hold there, {name}. That's the Wellspring behind me, and nobody goes into it alone. Not anymore. Folk who went down there on their own never came back up. Ask around the Ember and Anvil in Emberhold if you don't believe me; the regulars there have [stories].
dialogue.stories: Miners, first. Then a pair of trappers, then a boy on a dare. None of them came out. Something down there's gone bad, and it's souring the water with it. There's an old fisherman drinks at the Ember and Anvil who's been grumbling about that water for weeks. Talk to him.
dialogue.merrick: Merrick sent word? Then you're the one. I'll go down with you, {name}. Lead on into the cave; I'll be right behind you.
dialogue.unknown: I'm keeping watch, {name}. The cave stays closed to anyone going in alone.

merricks_line_sinew.hail: Merrick sent word about you, {name}. He says you're going down to the spring. Good. I'm going with you; lead on into the cave and I'll be right behind you.

merricks_line_spring.hail: The water's running clean again, {name}. Never thought I'd see it. The cave's yours to walk now.

watchman_corran.refuse_entry: Whoa, hold up, {name}! Nobody goes into that cave alone. Folk who go down there on their own don't come back. If you're set on it, go and listen to the regulars at the Ember and Anvil in Emberhold. Somebody there has more reason than most to want this cave put right.

corran_escort.name: Watchman Corran
corran_escort.title: Emberhold Watch
corran_escort.companion_join: Right behind you, {name}. You lead; I'll keep them off you. Sit when you need to, and I'll hold here till you're ready.
corran_escort.farewell: The spring's clean. My job here's done, {name}. I'll go tell Holt. Good work down there.

dialogue.hail: I'm with you, {name}. Lead the way, and I'll keep them off you.
dialogue.unknown: Keep your eyes open, {name}. I'm right behind you.

dialogue.hail: The pond, {name}! Bring the vial!
The crystal is wound in webs so thick you can barely see it. Under them, a weak blue light flickers, like something trying to breathe. Whatever holds it down, its heart beats close by.

merricks_line_spring.hail: The crystal shines clear and cold. The spring runs bright around it, all the way toward Greenmoor.

guildmaster.refuse: I train warriors, {name}. Soft hands like yours want Sister Anwen or the Magister. And if you're the sneaking kind, there's a woman in the back corner of the Ember and Anvil.

dialogue.hail: You there, {name}! Think you can hold a line? The Watch trains every [warrior] who can, and a few who can't.
dialogue.warrior: Steel, sweat and stubbornness. Come to me as you grow and I'll teach you to bandage yourself, to bash, and to roar. Press G to train.

guildmaster.refuse: The hearth calls whom it calls, {name}. You're not one of mine. Try Sergeant Brask or Magister Coyle, or, for your kind of work, the corner table at the Ember and Anvil.

dialogue.hail: Peace of the hearth to you, {name}. Those who [tend] it learn to mend what the wilds tear.
dialogue.tend: Clerics of the hearth heal, shield and, when we must, smite. As you grow, I'll teach you more. Press G to train.
dialogue.unknown: The Keeper knows more lore than I, {name}.

guildmaster.refuse: Hmm? Oh, no, no. I teach wizards. You want the Sergeant, or the Sister at the hearth. Or that shady one who drinks at the Ember and Anvil.

dialogue.hail: Ah, {name}. Careful, the ink's still wet. You've an interest in the [arcane]?
dialogue.arcane: Frost, fire, and the binding of limbs. I teach wizards who have survived long enough to be worth teaching. Press G to train.

tavern_keeper.name: Hessa Byrne
tavern_keeper.title: Keeper of the Ember and Anvil

dialogue.hail: Evening, {name}. Sit where you like. There's [ale], there's [stew], and there's [talk] if you'd rather have that.
dialogue.ale: Brewed in the cellar, and better than anything the Watch drinks. First one's on the house if you've come up from Greenmoor.
dialogue.stew: Mutton and barley. It's been on the fire since dawn, which is either a recommendation or a warning.
dialogue.talk: People come through here on their way to somewhere worse. If you're after [work], sit a while and someone will find you.
dialogue.work: Not mine to hand out. But the tables fill up after dark, and the ones who need something always end up telling me first.

dialogue.hail: Don't mind me, {name}. I've had this same seat for eleven years and I'll not be moved from it now. Unless you want to hear about the [cave].
dialogue.cave: The Wellspring, the old miners called it, up in Greenmoor's western hills. Men went in alone and never came out, and now the Watch keeps a guard on the mouth. Water's been sour ever since. Ask [Merrick] there; that one's been glaring into his ale over it for weeks.
dialogue.merrick: The grumpy one at the next table. Fished Greenmoor's pond for thirty years, and now nothing bites. Go on, say hello. Worst he'll do is growl at you.
dialogue.unknown: Hah. Ask Hessa, she knows everything worth knowing.

dialogue.hail: Quiet night, isn't it? Give me a copper and I'll make it less so.
dialogue.unknown: I only know songs about it, and the songs lie.

dialogue.hail: Well met, {name}. Few from Emberhold come this far up the vale. Mind the [wolves]; they've grown hungry and bold, and they are not the worst of what walks under these trees.
dialogue.wolves: Timber wolves, and the dire ones out of the deep woods, driven toward the road by something [worse]. Bring me four [wolf pelts] and I'll see you're paid for thinning the pack.
dialogue.wolf pelts: Four pelts, {name}. Hand them over when you have them. The first time, I'll throw in a pair of boots I've been stitching. After that it's coin, and my thanks.
dialogue.worse: Spiders, west of here, where the trees grow thick: [thornbacks]. Orcs to the east, the [Bloodtusk]. And in the north, the old [watchtower], where nothing living keeps the watch anymore.
dialogue.thornbacks: Their bite burns like nettle-fire. Their broodmother, Silkfang, nests in the deep woods west of the road. If you're brave enough to go near, bring me three lengths of [spider silk] and a venom sac.
dialogue.spider silk: Three lengths of thornback silk and one of their venom sacs. Silk that strong makes the finest gloves you'll ever wear, and the venom... well. A hermit has her uses for venom.
dialogue.bloodtusk: A clan of orcs camped east along the road. Raiders. Their warchief, Grolthar, wears the tusks of everything he's killed. Don't wander into that camp alone. Sergeant Harlan, on the road, pays for every orc tusk you bring him.
dialogue.watchtower: The Hollow Watch. Men of Emberhold once kept that tower. Now their bones keep it for them, and their captain, Veyl, still walks the walls. Something holds them there. I think it is his oath, sealed in the [signet] he wears.
dialogue.unknown: The trees say many things, {name}. That isn't one of them.
dialogue.signet: The captain's signet, the seal of the Watch. Take it from Veyl and bring it to me, {name}, and I'll bury it where the Watch can finally rest. I have something of his to give you in return.

dialogue.hail: Keep moving, {name}, and keep your blade loose. I walk this road from the obelisk to the [crossroads] and back, as far as the Watch reaches up here. Anything chases you, run to me.
dialogue.crossroads: Where the road splits east and west, past the river. East is [Bloodtusk] country. West, the trees close in and the spiders hang their webs. North is the old watchtower, and I don't go north.
dialogue.unknown: Ask the hermit, {name}. I just walk the road.
dialogue.bloodtusk: Orc raiders, camped east of the crossroads. The Watch pays for their [tusks]: every four you bring me is four fewer blades on my road. And their warchief, [Grolthar]... that's another matter.
dialogue.tusks: Four Bloodtusk tusks, {name}. Their raiders and shamans carry them. Bring me four and I'll pay you, every time.
dialogue.grolthar: Warchief Grolthar wears a necklace of tusks, one for everything he's killed. Some of those were Watchmen. Bring me that necklace and I'll give you my own blade for it.

shouts: Get off the road, you beast!
hunt_shouts: Back into the trees with you!
shouts_player: Halt, {name}! In the name of the Watch!

dialogue.hail: Mind the planks, {name}; the damp gets into everything out here. Welcome to Hollowmere. We fish, we mend our nets, and we keep one eye on the [water] and the other on the [ruins].
dialogue.water: The mere gives us perch and eel, and takes a boat or two a year. The worst of what lives in it is [Old Snapjaw], and the worst of what lives beside it are the [Mirescale].
dialogue.old snapjaw: A snapping turtle older than my grandmother, and as big as a rowboat. He suns himself on the middle island and bites through our nets like thread. Bring me his [shell] and the village will owe you.
dialogue.shell: The whole shell, {name}, so I know the old brute is truly gone. The first to bring it gets a shield our smith has waited years to make from it.
dialogue.snapjaw: Old Snapjaw, yes. His [shell], if you can get it.
dialogue.mirescale: Lizardfolk from the reed marsh on the western shore. They hunt anything that walks on two legs. Brina pays for their scales, if you've the stomach for it.
dialogue.ruins: There was a village on the south shore before ours. The mere rose one spring and took it, and took the people in their beds. They still walk there, the [drowned], and they walk farther after dark.
dialogue.drowned: Their captain, Maren, rings a [bell] beneath the water on moonless nights. We hear it through the planks. She rises only at night, among the ruins.
dialogue.bell: Bring me Maren's bell, and two of the lockets her people still wear, and we'll give them a proper burial at last. I'll give you a pearl the mere gave me as a girl. It's never brought me luck, but it might bring you some.
dialogue.unknown: I'm an old woman, {name}. Ask Brina; she hears everything that comes along the pier.

dialogue.hail: Oh! Didn't hear you on the boards. Brina, netmaker. If you're buying, I've arrows and bait and the best smoked perch this side of Emberhold. If you're hunting, I'm paying for [scales].
dialogue.scales: Mirescale scales. Tough as horn and they don't rot, so I weave them into the edges of the nets, where the [lizardfolk] and the turtles tear them. Four at a time, and I'll pay you each time.
dialogue.lizardfolk: The Mirescale. Their huts are in the reeds on the west shore, past the old road. Hunters, shamans that throw bog water hot enough to scald, and a chieftain, Ssrakka, who's never been seen to lose.
dialogue.unknown: Couldn't say, {name}. Try the Elder, at the end of the pier.

dialogue.hail: Stay on the boards after dark, {name}. I walk from the stone to the end of the pier and back; if anything follows you in, run to me.
dialogue.unknown: Ask the Elder, {name}. I just keep the pier.

dialogue.hail: Afternoon, {name}. Mind the ruts; the carts cut them deep this year. Harrow's Rest was the finest farmland outside Emberhold, before the [boars] and the [brigands].
dialogue.boars: Wild pigs, rooting up every row I plant, and the tusked ones will open your leg as soon as look at you. Bring me four [tusks] and I'll pay for every four.
dialogue.tusks: Four boar tusks, and I'll pay you each time. The first time, I've a pair of work gloves that'll do you better than they do me.
dialogue.brigands: Garrick the Red and his lot took the old Hallow farm in the southwest. They steal our seed, our tools, and anyone who walks the west road alone. Bring me Garrick's [ledger] and two of their red armbands, and I'll know it's done.
dialogue.ledger: He keeps a tally of everything he's taken from us. Bring it back with two of those red armbands, and you'll have the ring my father wore at every harvest.
dialogue.unknown: Couldn't tell you, {name}. Ask Marta, or Tilda at the stall.

dialogue.hail: You're new. Don't walk the fields after dark, {name}. Not since the [scarecrows] started walking.
dialogue.scarecrows: My husband stitched every one of them. After he died they started climbing off their posts at night. The worst of them is the big one in the south field, the one we called [Old Tatters].
dialogue.old tatters: He stood in the south field for thirty years. Now he walks it, but only at night. There's something inside him that shouldn't be. Bring me his [heart] and let my husband's work rest.
dialogue.heart: A bundle of straw, bound with red thread; my husband sewed one into every scarecrow for luck. Bring me Old Tatters' heart and I'll give you his hat. It's the only thing of his I can bear to part with.

dialogue.hail: Fresh bread, {name}, still warm! And arrows and stones for anyone going after those pigs. Press G if you want to see what I have.
dialogue.unknown: Oswin knows the farm business; I just sell the bread.

dialogue.hail: The Watch keeps a man out here since the brigands moved in, {name}. I walk from the green down the west road and back. Run to me if you're chased.

shouts_player: Halt, {name}! In the name of the Watch!

guildmaster.refuse: Me? I just like the corner, {name}. The Sergeant's by the gate, if you want a guild.

dialogue.hail: Sit, {name}, you're blocking my light. ...Ah. You're one of mine, or you want to be. The Watch calls us [thieves]; I call us the only ones in Emberhold who look behind things.
dialogue.thieves: Thieves, knives, whatever they like. We go where the Watch can't see: gnoll camps, orc tents, the dark behind a lizard's back. Learn to [hide] before you learn anything else.
dialogue.hide: Stand still in the shadows and they'll walk right past you. Move, and they won't. When you're older, I'll teach you to [sneak], and then the shadows move with you.
dialogue.sneak: Slow and quiet. Hidden and moving, you choose the fight, and the first blade goes in their back. That first strike from the dark hits twice as hard. Remember it.
dialogue.unknown: Couldn't say, {name}. Buy a drink and ask the keeper.

dialogue.hail: The Dawn-Tusk sees you, {name}. Few climb the Steps any more: the [shrines] above are guarded, and too many [pilgrims] never came down.
dialogue.shrines: Prabhagaj raised the sun in his trunk on the first morning, and his priests built a shrine on every step of the climb. The [guardians] they carved still keep them, and no longer know a pilgrim from a thief.
dialogue.guardians: Stone given a purpose and no judgment. At the Great Temple on the highest step stands the Dawn Colossus. Nothing living has passed it in a hundred years.
dialogue.pilgrims: They died on the climb and the sun dried them where they fell. Now they walk the old graveyard, the [Pilgrims' Rest], and their [tokens] are all that's left of who they were. Bring me four and I'll say their names at the dawn rite.
dialogue.tokens: Four pilgrims' tokens, {name}, as many times as you find them. The first time, take the boots I walked up here in; I won't be walking down.
dialogue.pilgrims' rest: The graveyard northwest of here. By day the dead are few. At night their high priest, [Sahkrin], rises among them.
dialogue.sahkrin: He led them up the Steps and promised them the sunrise. He's still leading them. Bring me his [scarab] and let them rest.
dialogue.scarab: A golden scarab he carried on his breast. Bring it to me and I'll give you the Dawn-Tusk's own pendant.
dialogue.unknown: I only know the Steps, {name}. Ask Dov about anything that can be bought.

dialogue.hail: Supplies up the Steps cost double, {name}; blame the [cult]. Press G if you're buying.
dialogue.cult: Fanatics in orange on the south terraces, worshipping a sun of their own making. They burn pilgrims who won't bow. Their leader, the [Hierophant], wears a mask like a burning sun.
dialogue.hierophant: Hierophant Vaur. Bring me that mask of his and three of their sigils, so the pilgrims know he's gone, and you can have the axe I've been saving for someone worth it.

dialogue.hail: Keep to the road, {name}. I walk from the stone to the first terrace; if anything follows you down, run to me.

hunt_shouts: Back up the Steps with you!

blesses.refuse: The Dawn-Tusk's light falls on everyone, {name}, but his blessing is for those who follow him. Your own god has gifts of their own.
blesses.wait: You've had his blessing within the hour, {name}. Let it wear off before you ask again.

dialogue.bind: Kneel, {name}, under the sun-disc. It is done: Prabhagaj will guide you home to Lanternhold.
dialogue.hail: Welcome to Lanternhold, {name}, and to the shrine of [Prabhagaj]. The lamps of the city are lit from the sun-disc in his trunk every dusk, and none has gone out in four hundred years. I can [bind] your soul to his shrine, if you'd have Lanternhold be your home.
dialogue.prabhagaj: The Dawn-Tusk, the elephant of first light. On the first morning he lifted the sun out of the dark in his trunk, and he has held it up every morning since. Nothing is hidden from him for long. Those who follow him may ask his [blessing] here.
dialogue.blessing: Only his followers may receive it.
dialogue.bindstone: This shrine is the bindstone of the Dawnstair. Fall anywhere in these lands and you wake at the elephant's feet.
dialogue.unknown: The Dawn-Tusk knows, {name}, but he hasn't told me.

guildmaster.refuse: Not my trade, {name}. Try the others round the plaza.

dialogue.hail: The Steps make warriors or bury them, {name}. If you're one of mine, I've things to teach you.
dialogue.unknown: Ask at the shrine, {name}; Dawnpriest Amaru knows the city best.

guildmaster.refuse: The light calls whom it calls, {name}; not you, not to me.

dialogue.hail: The Dawn-Tusk's light heals as well as it burns, {name}. Clerics, come and learn both.
dialogue.unknown: Ask at the shrine, {name}; Dawnpriest Amaru knows the city best.

guildmaster.refuse: Hmm? No. I teach wizards. Ask round the plaza.

dialogue.hail: Lightning and fire, {name}. Up here the air's thin enough to call both. If you're a wizard, sit.
dialogue.unknown: Ask at the shrine, {name}; Dawnpriest Amaru knows the city best.

guildmaster.refuse: I don't know you, {name}, and I'd like to keep it that way.

dialogue.hail: Lanterns everywhere, {name}, and still the shadows under them. Rogues, I'll teach you the rest.
dialogue.unknown: Ask at the shrine, {name}; Dawnpriest Amaru knows the city best.

dialogue.hail: The Lanternhold Exchange keeps accounts with the Hearthbank of Emberhold, {name}: what you left there, you'll find here.
Steel for the ones who hold the line, dawnweave for the ones who stand behind them, shadowleather for the ones behind everybody. Press G.
Steel from the mountain forges, {name}, sharpened on sunrise. Press G to see.
Welcome to Lanternhold, {name}. The lamps never go out here, and neither do we. Trouble on the Steps? Run for the gate.
Water first, {name}, questions after. Out here the sun kills slower than the [scorpions] and the [raiders], but it never stops trying.
dialogue.scorpions: Big as a cart and pale as the salt, so you step on them before you see them. Their stingers fetch a price in Lanternhold. Bring me four [stingers] and I'll pay each time.
dialogue.stingers: Four scorpion stingers, as often as you like. The first time, I've a pair of boots made for walking salt.
dialogue.raiders: The Salt Raiders, east, round a camp of stolen wagons. Their chief, [Vashti], blows a warhorn before every attack on a caravan.
dialogue.vashti: Vashti the Salt-Wolf. Bring me that warhorn of hers and the caravans will breathe again. You'll have the blade my best guard carried until the raiders took him.
dialogue.unknown: Ask Ibrem, {name}; he's been crossing the Bleach longer than I have.

dialogue.hail: Salt, water and steel, {name}, at desert prices. Press G. And if you're headed north, mind the [bones].
dialogue.bones: The Bleach is a graveyard. Something enormous died here before the first caravan, and its bones don't lie still: the bone giants walk out of them. The biggest of them, the [Titan], sits in the great ribcage north of the flats.
dialogue.titan: The Bone Titan. There's a heart in that cage of ribs that won't stop beating. Bring me the [heart] and I'll give you a talisman carved from its first bone.
dialogue.heart: The Heart of the Titan. It'll be heavy. Bring it anyway.

dialogue.hail: Keep close to the wagons, {name}. Anything follows you in, I'll handle it.

blesses.refuse: The rain falls on everyone, {name}, but the Tide-Trunked's blessing is for those who follow her. Your own god has gifts of their own.
blesses.wait: You've had her blessing within the hour, {name}. Let it wear off before you ask again.
blesses.give: Stand in the spray, {name}. ...There. Go gently.

dialogue.bind: Let her water touch your brow, {name}. There. Jalendra will carry you home to Rainhold when you call.
dialogue.hail: Welcome to Rainhold, {name}, and to the shrine of Jalendra, the Tide-Trunked. The rain never stops here; we stopped minding. Followers of hers may ask for her [blessing]. And if you're strong, there's a [storm] in the Throat I need quieted. I'll [bind] your soul to her basin, too, if you ask.
dialogue.storm: The Weeping Storm. A spirit of the monsoon gone wild, raging at the old temple in the Weeping Throat, north of the city. Bring me its [heart] and I'll give you a charm blessed at this shrine.
dialogue.heart: The Heart of the Storm. It will crackle in your hands. Bring it anyway.
dialogue.unknown: Ask the guildmasters, {name}, or Hunter Asha on the east pier.

guildmaster.refuse: Not my trade, {name}. Try the other halls.

dialogue.hail: The Throat is full of trolls that won't stay dead, {name}. Warriors, I'll teach you to keep hitting until they do.
dialogue.unknown: Ask at the shrine, {name}; Tidepriest Nalini knows the city best.

guildmaster.refuse: I don't know you, {name}. Keep walking.

dialogue.hail: Rain covers footsteps, {name}. If you're one of mine, come closer.
dialogue.unknown: Ask at the shrine, {name}; Tidepriest Nalini knows the city best.

guildmaster.refuse: The rain calls whom it calls, {name}; not you, not to me.

dialogue.hail: The Tide-Trunked heals as the rain does: slowly, everywhere. Clerics, come learn.
dialogue.unknown: Ask at the shrine, {name}; Tidepriest Nalini knows the city best.

guildmaster.refuse: Hmm? No. I teach wizards.

dialogue.hail: Lightning lives in every cloud over Rainhold, {name}. Wizards, sit, and I'll show you how to call it down.
dialogue.unknown: Ask at the shrine, {name}; Tidepriest Nalini knows the city best.

dialogue.hail: The Counting House keeps accounts with the Hearthbank of Emberhold, {name}: what you left there, you'll find here, dry.
Tidesteel doesn't rust, {name}, rainsilk doesn't soak, and sharkskin doesn't care. Press G.
Steel folded in rainwater, {name}. Press G to see.
Rain's good for fishing, {name}. Everything is, if you're patient. Press G for a pole and worms, then [fishing].
dialogue.fishing: Hold the pole, face the water, and right-click it, or type /fish. Every cast uses a worm. You'll get better the more you try. Bring me four [snapper] from the lagoon.
dialogue.snapper: Four lagoon snapper, as often as you like. The first time, I'll give you a slicker that keeps the rain off.
dialogue.unknown: Ask Hunter Asha about the Throat.
dialogue.tamu: Tamu sent you? With those needles? Then Tamu wants a net for another pack. Bring me the needles and two lagoon [snapper] for the oil, and I'll knot it.

dialogue.hail: You look like you can hunt, {name}. The Weeping Throat, north of the city, is full of [trolls] and worse. And there's an old [crocodile] I've been after for ten years.
dialogue.trolls: The Mudtooth trolls, in a camp of huts on the east bank of the river. They heal as fast as you cut them. Bring me four [tusks] and I'll pay you each time. Or bring me the stone crown of their chief, [Gorrak].
dialogue.tusks: Four troll tusks. As often as you like. The first time, gloves of troll hide: they knit themselves.
dialogue.gorrak: Gorrak Mudtooth. Bring me his stone crown and you'll have the blade of the last Tidewarden who went up there.
dialogue.crocodile: Old Graveljaw, in the swamp where the river spreads out in the southwest of the Throat. Bring me his [tooth].
dialogue.tooth: Graveljaw's tooth. Do that and I'll give you leggings of crocodile scale, from the one I did kill.

dialogue.hail: Welcome to Rainhold, {name}. Mind the planks, they're slick. Trouble on the road? Run for the piers.
Supplies for every trade, {name}: flour and spices for the [oven], thread and salts for [tailoring], herbs and vials for [alchemy], ore and a hammer for the [forge]. Press G to see.
dialogue.oven: Ovens bake, campfires roast. Put your ingredients in, press Combine. The Hearthside Cookbook tells you what goes with what.
dialogue.tailoring: A sewing kit's a bag you can combine in: tan your hides with salts, then stitch the leather with thread. Cloth wants the loom. My pattern book has the rest.
dialogue.alchemy: A mortar and pestle for potions, the brew barrel for the big draughts. Herbs and clear water in everything. The Alchemist's Notes are cheap.
dialogue.forge: Keep the hammer in the forge with the ore and a flask of water; it stays, the rest becomes metal. Bars first, then blades. The Smith's Handbook will set you straight.

dialogue.hail: Supplies for every trade, {name}: flour and spices for the [oven], thread and salts for [tailoring], herbs and vials for [alchemy], ore and a hammer for the [forge]. Press G to see.
dialogue.oven: Ovens bake, campfires roast. Put your ingredients in, press Combine. The Hearthside Cookbook tells you what goes with what.
