dialogue.forge: Keep the hammer in the forge with the ore and a flask of water; it stays, the rest becomes metal. Bars first, then blades. The Smith's Handbook will set you straight.

dialogue.hail: Supplies for every trade, {name}: flour and spices for the [oven], thread and salts for [tailoring], herbs and vials for [alchemy], ore and a hammer for the [forge]. Press G to see. And if you're new to the rain, ask me about a [rainproof pack].
dialogue.oven: Ovens bake, campfires roast. Put your ingredients in, press Combine. The Hearthside Cookbook tells you what goes with what.
dialogue.tailoring: A sewing kit's a bag you can combine in: tan your hides with salts, then stitch the leather with thread. Cloth wants the loom. My pattern book has the rest.
dialogue.alchemy: A mortar and pestle for potions, the brew barrel for the big draughts. Herbs and clear water in everything. The Alchemist's Notes are cheap.
dialogue.forge: Keep the hammer in the forge with the ore and a flask of water; it stays, the rest becomes metal. Bars first, then blades. The Smith's Handbook will set you straight.
dialogue.rainproof pack: Anything you carry in Rainhold gets wet, {name}, unless it's in a proper Rainhold pack: netted, oiled, toggled. I'll make you one. First I need netting needles, and bone makes the best. The skeletons in Greenmoor, east through the gate, are made of it. Bring me four bone chips.

guildmaster.refuse: The elements don't speak to everyone, {name}. Try the other guilds.

dialogue.hail: Earth, water, fire and air, {name}: each will answer a magician who asks properly. If you're one of mine, I'll teach you the asking. Your elementals will need [tending], too.
dialogue.tending: Mend the Bound heals your elemental; Stoke the Flame makes it quicker and harder-hitting. Tell it what to do from its window, or say /pet attack, back, follow, guard, sit, taunt. Earth holds a monster's attention, fire burns it down, water chills it, air staggers it.

guildmaster.refuse: The dead have nothing to say to you, {name}. Go back up the stairs.

dialogue.hail: You found the crypt, {name}. Good. The dead listen to those who are patient with them. Necromancers learn here, quietly, and the Watch pretends not to know.
dialogue.unknown: The dead keep their own counsel, {name}.

guildmaster.refuse: Not a magician? Then the flame is only warmth to you, {name}.

dialogue.hail: Up here the fire comes easily, {name}. Magicians, come: the higher callings are mine to teach.
dialogue.unknown: Ask at the shrine, {name}; Dawnpriest Amaru knows the city best.

guildmaster.refuse: I prepare the dead, {name}. You aren't one of mine, and you aren't dead. Yet.

dialogue.hail: I lay out the city's dead, {name}. Some of them get up again, for the right teacher. Necromancer? Then sit.
dialogue.unknown: Ask at the shrine, {name}; Dawnpriest Amaru knows the city best.

guildmaster.refuse: The tide answers magicians, {name}, and you're not one.

dialogue.hail: The rain is full of water elementals, {name}, if you know how to call them out. Magicians, I'll teach you the deeper calls.
dialogue.unknown: Ask at the shrine, {name}; Tidepriest Nalini knows the city best.

guildmaster.refuse: Bones are for necromancers, {name}. Move along.

dialogue.hail: The lagoon gives up its drowned, {name}, and I give them work. Necromancers, I'll teach you what the river taught me.
dialogue.unknown: Ask at the shrine, {name}; Tidepriest Nalini knows the city best.

guildmaster.refuse: The spirits haven't spoken your name to me, {name}. Try the others round the hearth.

dialogue.hail: Sit a while, {name}. The spirits walk close to the hearth here. Shamans learn from me: how to slow a beast's blows, how to lend a friend the bear's strength, how to mend a wound slowly and well.
dialogue.unknown: The spirits don't answer that one, {name}. Ask Keeper Maelin at the hearth.

guildmaster.refuse: You don't walk with spirits, {name}. The other guilds are round the plaza.

dialogue.hail: The dawn wakes more than the sun, {name}. Shamans, come learn what the old spirits of the Dawnstair still teach.

guildmaster.refuse: The rain speaks to shamans, {name}, and you're not one.

dialogue.hail: Listen: every drop is a voice, {name}. Shamans who hear them come to me, and I teach them to answer.
dialogue.unknown: Ask at the shrine, {name}; Tidepriest Nalini knows the city best.

dialogue.hail: Peace, {name}. I kept the lowest shrine when the others went up to the monastery and did not come down. They are the [Fallen] now, and the terraces are [overrun].
dialogue.fallen: My brothers. The [abbot], Varun, swore the Dawn-Tusk had abandoned us and that we would wake the old [guardians] ourselves. They broke their vows to do it. Each of them still wears the order's beads. Bring me their [beads], four at a time, and I will say the rites for them.
dialogue.beads: Four tarnished prayer beads, {name}. Every four I purify is a brother at rest. The first time, take my old hand wraps; they are all I have left of the order.
dialogue.abbot: Abbot Varun the Unbound, at the top of the terraces in the monastery hall. He carries the order's [seal].
dialogue.seal: Bring me the Abbot's Seal and I will lay it on the Dawn-Tusk's altar. Then the order can end with some grace. I will give you the beads I have worn since I was a boy.
dialogue.guardians: The stone watchers of the monastery: gargoyles on the pillars, golems in the courts. Varun woke them, and one he woke is a [colossus].
dialogue.colossus: The Terrace Colossus walks the highest court. Its heart is a stone that still remembers the dawn. Bring me its [heartstone] and I will have it set in a ring for you.
dialogue.heartstone: The Colossus's heartstone. Nothing smaller will do, {name}.
dialogue.overrun: [Harpies] on the upper steps, griffons riding the wind above them, snow leopards in the tea, trolls in the high passes. Ask Pema; she knows the terraces better than I do.
dialogue.unknown: The terraces have many voices, {name}. That is not one I know.

dialogue.hail: Sit, {name}, drink. Tea from the lowest terrace, the only one we still pick. The [harpies] took the rest. Press G if you're buying.
dialogue.harpies: Screeching things, nesting on the upper steps. They carry off the pickers. Bring me four [talons] and I'll pay you, every time.
dialogue.talons: Four harpy talons, {name}. I grind them for the pickers' charms, not that the charms work.
dialogue.griffons: The griffons were here before the monastery. Their matriarch, [Skyrend], nests on the high cliff and hunts the whole mountain.
dialogue.skyrend: Skyrend the Matriarch. Bring me one of her plumes and I'll make you a cloak that sheds the wind.
dialogue.plume: Skyrend's plume, {name}. Only the matriarch's will do.
dialogue.unknown: Ask Brother Tenzin, dear. He knows old things.

dialogue.hail: Stay near the rest, {name}. The harpies don't come this low, and neither do the monks.

hunt_shouts: Back up the terraces with you!

dialogue.hail: You came up from Thornwood? Then you've seen the ash. Forgehold sent us to watch the pass, {name}, and what we watch is the [Ember] cult.
dialogue.ember: Madmen who say Agnavar's fire should burn the world clean. They've a fortified camp in the east of the pass, and every one of them carries an [ember sigil]. Their [leader] rules it from the fire.
dialogue.ember sigil: Four sigils, {name}, and I'll pay for each four, as often as you bring them. The first time, you'll have a scout's signet.
dialogue.sigils: Four sigils, {name}, and I'll pay for each four.
dialogue.leader: High Pyromancer [Ashkar]. He brands his cultists with an iron he keeps at his belt.
dialogue.ashkar: Bring me Ashkar's [brand] and the cult loses its heart. I'll give you a blade forged in Forgehold's own fire.
dialogue.brand: Ashkar's brand, {name}. Nothing else proves he's dead.

dialogue.hail: Emberforged steel, {name}, quenched in the lava itself. Nothing finer this side of Forgehold. Press G if you're buying. And if you're hunting, I'll pay for [drake] scales.
dialogue.drake: Ash drakes, in the lava fields west of the road. Their scales make the best quench-shields. Four [scales] and I'll pay, every time. And if you're very brave, there's [Cindermaw].
dialogue.cindermaw: Cindermaw. The great drake of the pass, nesting at the top of the lava falls. Bring me its [heart] and I'll give you a cloak of its kin's scales.
dialogue.heart: Cindermaw's heart. Still warm, I'd wager.

dialogue.hail: Stay close to the outpost, {name}. The ash hides things.

hunt_shouts: Back into the ash with you!

guildmaster.refuse: You don't carry a bow like a ranger, {name}. The other guilds are round the hearth.

dialogue.hail: Rangers learn from me, {name}: the bow, the blade, and the wild's own quiet magic. The wild is patient; learn to be.

guildmaster.refuse: Not a ranger? Then ask round the plaza.

dialogue.hail: The dawn lights the hunter's way, {name}. Rangers, come and learn the bow as the Dawnstair's wardens shoot it.

guildmaster.refuse: The reeds only speak to rangers, {name}.

dialogue.hail: In the rain, a ranger's ears matter more than their eyes, {name}. Rangers, I'll teach you to hear the jungle.
Mind the channels, {name}; the mud takes boots and the reeds take the rest. We cut reed for Rainhold's roofs, when the [pondkin] let us.
dialogue.pondkin: Frog-folk. They think every reed in the mere is theirs, and they spear anyone who says otherwise. Their mudcallers carry [fetishes], bone and shell; bring me four and I'll pay, every time.
dialogue.fetishes: Four pondkin fetishes, {name}. The first time, I've a pair of boots that don't sink.
dialogue.bloatking: Their king. A great fat thing on a throne of mud in the northwest, wearing a crown of rust and shells. Bring me his [crown] and the reed beds are ours again.
dialogue.crown: Bloatking Ghurr's crown, {name}. Nothing else will convince the others.
dialogue.unknown: Ask Kesh at the boats, or the priestess.

dialogue.hail: Boats, bait, bread, {name}. Press G. And if you're hunting, I'll pay for [reedstalker] plumes.
dialogue.reedstalker: The giant herons. Their plumes make the best fletching in the Monsoon. Four [plumes], and I'll pay every time.
dialogue.stilt-legs: Old Stilt-Legs, the great heron of the rookery in the northeast. Bring me one of its [plume] and I'll make you a cloak.
dialogue.plume: Old Stilt-Legs' plume. Only that one.

dialogue.hail: Jalendra's peace, {name}. Veyamar drowned in one night of rain, long ago; its people still walk the water. The [Sunken] cannot rest, and the [coven] makes it worse.
dialogue.sunken: Each of the Sunken wears the village charm. Bring me four [charms] and I will sing them to Jalendra, and the water will let them go.
dialogue.charms: Four sunken charms, {name}. As many times as you can bear it.
dialogue.headwoman: Headwoman Ishani walks at night, among the ruins of her hall. She wears a [lotus] in her hair; bring it to me and her people will follow her to rest.
dialogue.coven: The Sedge Sisters, witches in the southwest fen, who raise the bog against us. Their mother, Marrowroot, keeps her [heart] in a jar, they say.
dialogue.heart: Mother Marrowroot's heart. Bring it, and the coven breaks.
dialogue.unknown: Jalendra hears all, {name}. I do not.

dialogue.hail: Stay by the camp, {name}. The reeds hide more than frogs.
Welcome to Drownfast, {name}, the citadel of the Tide Kings. Rainhold sent us to learn why the storm never ends. The [Tidesworn] still guard their walls.
dialogue.tidesworn: The drowned garrison. Every one of them wears the royal [insignia]. Bring me four and Rainhold pays, every time.
dialogue.insignia: Four tidesworn insignias, {name}. The first time, a blade from our armory.
dialogue.king: Tideking Varundra, the last of them, holds the throne in the sea temple. I think the storm is his grief. Bring me his [crown].
dialogue.crown: Varundra's crown, {name}. Then maybe the rain will stop.

dialogue.hail: I dive for pearls in the old harbor, {name}, when the [naga] let me.
dialogue.naga: Serpent-folk, come up from the deeps into the drowned halls. Their scales fetch a fine price. Four [scales], every time.
dialogue.queen: Queen Sessavi. She wears the greatest pearl of the deeps on her brow. Bring me that [pearl] and I'll set it for you.

dialogue.hail: The storm is alive, {name}, and it has children: the [tempest] spirits. Press G for supplies.
dialogue.tempest: Bring me four tempest [shards] and I'll pay; I read the storm in them.
dialogue.warden: The Stormbound Warden, chained to the great tower. Bring me its [chain] and I'll forge you something storm-proof.
dialogue.chitterjaw: Old Chitterjaw, the great crab of the causeways. Its [claw] would make a shield nothing could break.

dialogue.hail: Keep to the causeways, {name}.
Welcome to Dewstep, {name}, the first step below Lanternhold. We pick the city's tea here, when the [moths] and the [monkeys] let us.
dialogue.moths: Lantern moths. They come to our lamps at dusk and lay their eggs in the young leaves. Bring me four of their [wings] and I'll pay for every four.
dialogue.wings: Four lantern moth wings, {name}. The first time, I've a pair of garden sandals for you.
dialogue.monkeys: A troop of thieving monkeys in the old orchard east of the road. They snatch baskets, bangles, anything bright, and their king, [Pilfer], is the worst of them.
dialogue.pilfer: Pilfer the Troop-King. He wears a bangle he stole from the tea house itself. Bring me his [bangle] and two of the trinkets his troop took, and I'll give you something bright of your own.
dialogue.bangle: Pilfer's bangle and two stolen trinkets, {name}.
dialogue.unknown: Ask Kaveri about the beasts, Brother Ravi about the old shrine, or Warden Tashi about the Dustpaw.
dialogue.moti: Moti's making another satchel? Then you'll need the body stitched. Bring me his thread and two jackal pelts from the west fields, and I'll do it.

dialogue.hail: Keep your eyes on the grass, {name}. [Jackals] hunt the west meadows and [cobras] sun on the southern rocks.
dialogue.jackals: They run in packs and they're bold. Bring me three jackal [pelts]; I'll pay for every three.
dialogue.pelts: Three jackal pelts, {name}. The first time, I'll give you leggings sewn from them.
dialogue.cobras: Hooded cobras, in the rocks south of the river. Bring me three cobra [fangs]; the healers in the city want the venom.
dialogue.fangs: Three cobra fangs. The first time, a dagger with a fang for its point.
dialogue.tigers: Young tigers in the southwest woods, and their mother, [Amberstripe], who has killed three pickers this year.
dialogue.amberstripe: The old tigress. Bring me one of her [fang] and I'll make you a mantle of her kin's stripes.

dialogue.hail: Dawn's blessing on you, {name}. West of the road stands an old [shrine] of Prabhagaj, broken long ago. It isn't at rest.
dialogue.shrine: Little lights drift around it by day, lantern [wisps]. At night the hungry dead come looking for offerings no one leaves anymore, and the [widow] walks among them.
dialogue.wisps: Bring me three wisp [lights]. I keep them in a jar and pray over them; it quiets them. I'll give you prayer beads, the first time.
dialogue.widow: A woman who waited at that shrine with her lantern for a husband who never came home. She waits still. Bring me her [lantern] and I'll lay her to rest.
dialogue.lantern: The Widow's Lantern. Only at night will you find her.

dialogue.hail: Tea, bread, bait, {name}. Press G to trade. And every picker needs a [satchel].
dialogue.unknown: I only sell things. Ask Anjali.
dialogue.satchel: A tea-picker's satchel: light, tough, and it never snags a leaf. I'll make you one, but I'm out of thread. Lantern moth wings spin into the finest silk there is. Bring me four.

dialogue.hail: Stay near the lanterns, {name}. The [Dustpaw] have been raiding the pickers again.
dialogue.dustpaw: Jackal-folk, from the dry country. They've a camp in the southeast past the paddies. Bring me four of their bead [strings] and I'll pay, every time.
dialogue.strings: Four Dustpaw bead strings. The first time, a buckler from our stores.
dialogue.rattlejaw: Their chief, Chief Rattlejaw. He wears a necklace of trophies. Bring me his [necklace] and they'll scatter.

dialogue.hail: You made it through Cinderpass, {name}. Welcome to the Burn, what's left of it. Forgehold holds this camp against the [giants].
dialogue.giants: Ember giants, down from the mountain's heart. They smith in the east, in a hall older than our city. Their hearts burn like forge coal; bring me four heart-[coals] and I'll pay, every time.
dialogue.coals: Four giant's heart-coals, {name}. The first time, gauntlets from my own forge.
dialogue.thane: Their thane, Korrok Emberhand. He wears an iron [crown] that never cools. Bring it to me.
dialogue.crown: The thane's iron crown, {name}. Mind your hands.
dialogue.unknown: Ask Mott about the town, Ilse about the hounds, Omari about the birds.

dialogue.hail: Tallpine was my town, {name}. Loggers and sawyers, west of the road. Then the fire came, and the [imps] came with it.
dialogue.imps: Fire imps. They dance in the ruins and cackle while they burn what's left. Bring me four imp [horns]; I'll pay each time.
dialogue.horns: Four imp horns, {name}. The first time, my old signet from the mill.
dialogue.smoke: The smoke that walks. It came out of the vents with them. Bring me three bottles of it, [bottled] smoke, and I'll weave you something.
dialogue.bottled: Three bottles of smoke. Stopper them quick.
dialogue.cackleflame: Their lord, Cackleflame, sits in my sawmill like a king. Bring me his [lordly] crown.

dialogue.hail: Keep to the road, {name}. The [firehounds] run the plains in packs, and ash wolves run with them.
dialogue.firehounds: Their manes burn. Bring me three [manes] and I'll pay every time.
dialogue.manes: Three firehound manes, {name}. The first time, a mantle sewn from them.
dialogue.ashmaw: The pack's alpha, Ashmaw. Bring me his burning [mane] and I'll give you a pendant of his fangs.

dialogue.hail: Agnavar's fire burned this forest, {name}, and his [firebirds] nest in what's left. Supplies too, if you need them: press G.
dialogue.firebirds: Birds of living flame. Bring me four [feathers] and I'll pay each time.
dialogue.feathers: Four firebird feathers. The first time, a cap sewn with them.
dialogue.phoenix: Pyrelle the Undying, the great phoenix of the north. Kill her and she burns to [ember], and rises again. Bring me the ember.
dialogue.ember: The phoenix's ember, {name}. Quickly, before she rises.

dialogue.hail: Stay by the fires, {name}.
Welcome to Forgehold, {name}, and to the fire of [Agnavar] that has not gone out since the mountain was young. I can [bind] your soul to his flame.
dialogue.agnavar: The Ember-Tusked. He struck the first spark in the mountain's heart, and we have kept it. His followers may ask for his [blessing] once an hour.
dialogue.bind: Stand in the heat, {name}. There: Agnavar will bring you home to Forgehold.
dialogue.unknown: Ask the guildmasters round the plaza.

blesses.refuse: Agnavar's fire warms everyone, {name}, but his blessing is for those who follow him.
blesses.wait: You've had his blessing within the hour, {name}.
blesses.give: Hold out your hands, {name}. ...Feel it? Go and burn bright.

dialogue.hail: Steel and fire made this city, {name}. If you fight, I'll teach you.
dialogue.unknown: Ask Flamekeeper Ashani at the shrine.

guildmaster.refuse: Not my craft, {name}. The others are round the plaza.

dialogue.hail: Healing in a city of forges, {name}: there's never a shortage of burns. Cleric? Come.
dialogue.unknown: Ask Flamekeeper Ashani at the shrine.

guildmaster.refuse: Not my craft, {name}. The others are round the plaza.

dialogue.hail: Fire is only the first element, {name}. Wizard? I have spells for you.
dialogue.unknown: Ask Flamekeeper Ashani at the shrine.

guildmaster.refuse: Not my craft, {name}. The others are round the plaza.

dialogue.hail: Smoke hides everything here, {name}. One of mine? Then listen.
dialogue.unknown: Ask Flamekeeper Ashani at the shrine.

guildmaster.refuse: Not my craft, {name}. The others are round the plaza.

dialogue.hail: Every forge here has an elemental in it, {name}. Magician? Let's call yours.
dialogue.unknown: Ask Flamekeeper Ashani at the shrine.

guildmaster.refuse: Not my craft, {name}. The others are round the plaza.

dialogue.hail: The dead of Blackglass don't rest, {name}. Neither do we. Necromancer?
dialogue.unknown: Ask Flamekeeper Ashani at the shrine.

guildmaster.refuse: Not my craft, {name}. The others are round the plaza.

dialogue.hail: The spirits of the mountain are loud here, {name}. Shaman? Sit by me.
dialogue.unknown: Ask Flamekeeper Ashani at the shrine.

guildmaster.refuse: Not my craft, {name}. The others are round the plaza.

dialogue.hail: The Burn is a hard hunting ground, {name}. Ranger? I've tricks for it.
dialogue.unknown: Ask Flamekeeper Ashani at the shrine.

guildmaster.refuse: Not my craft, {name}. The others are round the plaza.

dialogue.hail: The Forgehold Vault keeps accounts with every bank in the land, {name}.
Supplies for every trade, {name}, and the forges are right there. Press G.
Magmasteel for the front, emberhide for the quick, flameweave for the ones who burn things. Press G.
Forged in Agnavar's own fire, {name}. Press G.
Blackglass is the finest glass in the world, {name}, and the [golems] won't let us near it.
dialogue.golems: Glass golems. Something woke them. Their cores are pure glass; bring me four [cores] and I'll pay every time.
dialogue.cores: Four glass golem cores. The first time, a pair of my own lenses.
dialogue.colossus: The Black Colossus, in the middle of the fields. Bring me its [heart].

dialogue.hail: The [drakes] of Blackglass nest among the spires in the northwest, {name}. They take our miners.
dialogue.drakes: Obsidian drakes. Their scales turn blades. Bring me three [scales], every time.
dialogue.scales: Three obsidian drake scales. The first time, leggings of their scales.
dialogue.vitrax: Vitrax, the obsidian wyrm, their mother. Bring me her [eye].

dialogue.hail: Glass [spiders] spin silk that's half glass, {name}. I make wonders from it, when I can get it.
dialogue.spiders: In the shard spires, northeast. Bring me three spools of their [silk], every time.
dialogue.silk: Three spools of glass spider silk. The first time, gloves woven with it.
dialogue.shardmother: Their queen, the Shardmother. Her [crown] of shards would make a fine blade.

dialogue.hail: An old army died in Blackglass, {name}, when the valley melted. At night they [rise] from the glass.
dialogue.rise: The glassbound. Bring me four of their [insignia] and I'll pay each time; their families deserve them back.
dialogue.insignia: Four glassbound insignia. The first time, greaves from our armory.
dialogue.aldric: Captain Aldric led them. He carries their banner still. Bring me his [banner] and let them rest.

dialogue.hail: Welcome to Forgehold, {name}. Mind the lava.
Welcome to Dawnwatch, {name}, the Dawn-Tusk's high fort. We've held these walls through a winter of siege. The [ogres] are at our gates.
dialogue.unknown: Ask the Beacon-Keeper, or the Falconer.
dialogue.ogres: Stonebrow ogres, a whole warband with siege engines. Bring me four of their [tusks] and I'll pay, every time.
dialogue.tusks: Four Stonebrow tusks, {name}. The first time, a bracer from our armory.
dialogue.uthrak: Their warlord, Uthrak Stonebrow. His war horn calls the assault. Bring me his [horn].

dialogue.hail: The beacon must never go out, {name}. The [spirits] of the mountain want it dark.
dialogue.spirits: Snow spirits and avalanches that walk. Bring me four breaths of [frozen] air from them; I burn them in the beacon, every time.
dialogue.frozen: Four frozen breaths, {name}. The first time, a ring.
dialogue.storm-crowned: The Storm-Crowned, their lord, on the high snowfields. Bring me a [shard] of its crown.
dialogue.shard: A shard of the Storm Crown, {name}.

dialogue.hail: The [rocs] and wyverns of these crags take our birds and our sentries, {name}.
dialogue.rocs: Bring me three roc [feathers], every time.
dialogue.feathers: Three roc feathers. The first time, a cloak of them.
dialogue.sunwing: Sunwing, the great roc of the western crags. Bring me her golden [plume].

dialogue.hail: Our own dead walk the old outer walls at night, {name}: the [sentinels] who fell when the fort was young.
dialogue.sentinels: Bring me their sun-[badges], four at a time, and I'll lay them in the chapel.
dialogue.badges: Four sentinels' sun-badges, {name}. The first time, a pendant.
dialogue.halvard: Knight-Commander Halvard leads them still. Bring me his sun [banner] and they'll rest.

dialogue.hail: Stores for the siege, {name}. Press G.
Keep your head down, {name}; the catapults are loaded.
The Mirror Flats, {name}: step lightly, the water's only ankle deep. The [skiff] raiders come fast across it.
dialogue.unknown: Ask the others at the camp.
dialogue.skiff: Duneskiff raiders. Bring me four of their [veils], every time.
dialogue.veils: Four nomad veils. The first time, a sash.
dialogue.asra: Their queen, Asra of the Skiffs. Bring me her salt [crown].

dialogue.hail: The flats remember everyone who crosses them, {name}, and sometimes the [reflections] step out.
dialogue.reflections: Mirror images of travelers long gone. Bring me four mirror [shards] from them, every time.
dialogue.shards: Four mirror shards. The first time, gloves.
dialogue.reflection: The oldest of them, the Reflection. Bring me its cracked [face].

dialogue.hail: I cut salt, {name}, and the [crabs] cut me.
dialogue.crabs: Salt crabs, big as carts. Bring me four [claws], every time.
dialogue.claws: Four salt crab claws. The first time, boots.
dialogue.saltclaw: Old Saltclaw, the biggest. There's a salt pearl in him. Bring me the [pearl].

dialogue.hail: Waders and sky [rays], {name}; the flats are alive if you look.
dialogue.rays: Bring me four wader [plumes] and I'll pay, every time.
dialogue.plumes: Four wader plumes. The first time, a cap.
dialogue.great: The great sky ray glides the north flats. Bring me its [spine].

dialogue.hail: Salt, water, bread, {name}. Press G.
The Reach is Rainhold's rice bowl, {name}, when the [whiskerfolk] let us fish it.
dialogue.unknown: Ask the others at the landing.
dialogue.whiskerfolk: Catfish-folk, and the hippos they herd. Bring me four [barbels], every time.
dialogue.barbels: Four whiskerfolk barbels. The first time, a belt.
dialogue.king: The River King, crowned in pearls. Bring me his pearl [crown].

dialogue.hail: The [mudfolk] dam our channels, {name}, and the fish go elsewhere.
dialogue.mudfolk: Little diggers of mud. Bring me four mud [charms], every time.
dialogue.charms: Four mud charms. The first time, a bracelet.
dialogue.gloop: Their mud-shaman, Gloop. Bring me his shell [mask].

dialogue.hail: Serpents in every channel, {name}, and [swarms] above them.
dialogue.swarms: Never mind the swarms. Bring me four serpent [scales], every time.
dialogue.scales: Four delta serpent scales. The first time, gloves.
dialogue.coilmother: Old Coilmother, the great serpent of the east channels. Bring me her [fang].

dialogue.hail: The smugglers' barges sank in the silt, {name}, and the [smugglers] never left them.
dialogue.smugglers: Drowned smugglers. Bring me four of their [tokens], every time.
dialogue.tokens: Four smuggler's tokens. The first time, coin enough.
dialogue.blackwater: Captain Wren Blackwater kept a ledger of every debt in Rainhold. Bring me the [ledger].

dialogue.hail: Nets, bait, bread, {name}. Press G.
Tidemouth holds, {name}, for now. The [Saltreavers] come every tide.
dialogue.saltreavers: Sea raiders from over the horizon. Bring me four of their [arm-rings], every time.
dialogue.arm-rings: Four reaver arm-rings. The first time, one for your own arm.
dialogue.saltbeard: Their king, Harrow Saltbeard. Bring me his whalebone [crown].

dialogue.hail: The [storms] come off the sea to put out my light, {name}.
dialogue.storms: Storm spirits. Bring me four bottles of [lightning], every time.
dialogue.lightning: Four bottles of lightning. The first time, coin enough.
dialogue.tempest: The Tempest Lord, who rules them. Bring me its [heart].

dialogue.hail: There are [clawfolk] under the docks, {name}, and worse below them.
dialogue.clawfolk: Crab-men. Bring me four [pincers], every time.
dialogue.pincers: Four clawfolk pincers. The first time, a shield of their shell.
dialogue.horror: The Horror Below, in the deep water past the point. Bring me its glowing [lure].

dialogue.hail: Sea [serpents] in the bay, gulls the size of dogs, {name}. A harpooner's paradise.
dialogue.serpents: Bring me four sea serpent [scales], every time.
dialogue.scales: Four sea serpent scales. The first time, leggings.
dialogue.whitefin: Leviathan Whitefin, the great serpent of the bay. Bring me its [fin].

dialogue.hail: Rope, tar, bread, arrows, {name}. Press G.
Stay behind the barricades, {name}.
Welcome to Windbreak, {name}. Mind the edges; the wind takes the careless. And the [Kitewing] take the rest.
dialogue.kitewing: Sky-bandits who glide between the mesas on kites. Bring me four scraps of their kite [silk], every time.
dialogue.silk: Four scraps of kite silk. The first time, a sash of it.
dialogue.tarn: Their chief, Tarn Kitewing, flies a painted sail. Bring me the [sail].

dialogue.hail: The stone [giants] stack their cairns against the wind, {name}, and crush anyone who knocks one down.
dialogue.giants: Bring me four of their hand-[stones], every time.
dialogue.stones: Four giant's hand-stones. The first time, a pendant.
dialogue.stackstone: Old Stackstone, their elder. Bring me his [capstone].

dialogue.hail: The winds here are alive, {name}: gale [spirits], dust devils, and worse.
dialogue.spirits: Bring me four gale [essences], every time.
dialogue.essences: Four gale essences. The first time, a bracer.
dialogue.storm-eye: The Storm-Eye, the great cyclone of the east mesas. Bring me its [heart].

dialogue.hail: Giant eagles and [thunderbirds] nest on the spires, {name}. Beautiful, and deadly.
dialogue.thunderbirds: Bring me four eagle [talons], every time.
dialogue.talons: Four giant eagle talons. The first time, a ring.
dialogue.skarrow: Skarrow, the great thunderbird. Bring me her [crest].

dialogue.hail: Supplies, {name}. Press G.
Keep back from the edge, {name}.
Welcome to Galehold, {name}, where the wind never stops and neither do we. This is the shrine of [Vayuketh]; I can [bind] your soul to it.
dialogue.vayuketh: He Who Breathes the Plains. His ears are the sails of the world. His followers may ask for his [blessing] once an hour.
dialogue.bind: Stand in the wind, {name}. There: Vayuketh will blow you home to Galehold.
dialogue.unknown: Ask the guildmasters round the square.

blesses.refuse: The wind blows for everyone, {name}, but Vayuketh's breath is for his own.
blesses.wait: You've had his breath within the hour, {name}.
blesses.give: Breathe in, {name}. ...Deeper. Go where the wind takes you.

dialogue.hail: A warrior has to stand against the wind, {name}. Mine? Then stand.
dialogue.unknown: Ask Windspeaker Sabine at the shrine.

guildmaster.refuse: Not my trade, {name}. The others are round the square.

dialogue.hail: Healing on the wind, {name}. Cleric? I have prayers for you.
dialogue.unknown: Ask Windspeaker Sabine at the shrine.

guildmaster.refuse: Not my trade, {name}. The others are round the square.

dialogue.hail: The sky is full of power, {name}, if you know how to pull it down. Wizard?
dialogue.unknown: Ask Windspeaker Sabine at the shrine.

guildmaster.refuse: Not my trade, {name}. The others are round the square.

dialogue.hail: The wind covers every footstep here, {name}. One of mine?
dialogue.unknown: Ask Windspeaker Sabine at the shrine.

guildmaster.refuse: Not my trade, {name}. The others are round the square.

dialogue.hail: Air elementals were born here, {name}. Magician? Let's call yours.
dialogue.unknown: Ask Windspeaker Sabine at the shrine.

guildmaster.refuse: Not my trade, {name}. The others are round the square.

dialogue.hail: The barrows of the Long Grass are full, {name}. Necromancer?
dialogue.unknown: Ask Windspeaker Sabine at the shrine.

guildmaster.refuse: Not my trade, {name}. The others are round the square.

dialogue.hail: The spirits ride the wind, {name}. Shaman? Sit by me.
dialogue.unknown: Ask Windspeaker Sabine at the shrine.

guildmaster.refuse: Not my trade, {name}. The others are round the square.

dialogue.hail: The plains are the finest hunting in the world, {name}. Ranger?
dialogue.unknown: Ask Windspeaker Sabine at the shrine.

guildmaster.refuse: Not my trade, {name}. The others are round the square.

dialogue.hail: The Counting-House keeps accounts with every bank in the land, {name}.
Supplies for every trade, {name}. Press G.
Skyforged steel, windrunner leather, galeweave for the casters. Press G.
Blades that sing in the wind, {name}. Press G.
East of the gate the grass runs to the sky, {name}, and the [Hoofborn] ride it.
dialogue.hoofborn: Horse-folk raiders. Bring me four horsetail [braids], every time.
dialogue.braids: Four horsetail braids. The first time, a charm.
dialogue.oruk: Khan Oruk, who leads them. Bring me his horsetail [banner].

dialogue.hail: Things [stalk] the Long Grass, {name}. You won't see them until they want you to.
dialogue.stalk: Grass stalkers and howlers. Bring me four [pelts], every time.
dialogue.pelts: Four grass stalker pelts. The first time, boots.
dialogue.tawnyjaw: Tawnyjaw, the man-eater. Bring me her [fang].

dialogue.hail: The great [herds] feed half this city, {name}, when they aren't trampling it.
dialogue.herds: Bring me four thunderhoof [horns], every time.
dialogue.horns: Four thunderhoof horns. The first time, gauntlets of horn.
dialogue.herd-king: Old Thunderhoof, the herd-king. Bring me his [horn].

dialogue.hail: The old horse-lords lie in [barrows] in the north grass, {name}, and at night they rise.
dialogue.barrows: Bring me four pieces of barrow [bronze], every time.
dialogue.bronze: Four pieces of barrow bronze. The first time, greaves.
dialogue.lord: The Barrow Lord, the first of them. Bring me his death [mask].
dialogue.mask: The Barrow Lord's death mask, {name}. At night.

dialogue.hail: Welcome to Galehold, {name}. Hold on to your hat.
You stand at the Hearth of Agnavar, {name}, where the first fire still burns. The [court] of the ember giants holds the north-east.
dialogue.unknown: Ask the others at the rest.
dialogue.court: The ember court, armored giants who serve their queen. Bring me four of their [signets], every time.
dialogue.signets: Four ember court signets. The first time, a bracer.
dialogue.brannagh: Queen Brannagh, who would rule the flame itself. Bring me her molten [crown].

dialogue.hail: The [salamanders] tend the flame in their own way, {name}, and they kill pilgrims who come near.
dialogue.salamanders: Fire-lizard folk from the south-east dens. Bring me four of their [scales], every time.
dialogue.scales: Four salamander scales. The first time, boots.
dialogue.scorchtongue: Scorchtongue, their high priest. Bring me his [brazier].

dialogue.hail: Agnavar's fire makes [elementals] as easily as it makes steel, {name}.
dialogue.elementals: Greater fire elementals and living magma. Bring me four hearts of [flame], every time.
dialogue.flame: Four hearts of flame. The first time, a ring.
dialogue.forgeheart: The Living Forgeheart, lord of them all, at the great forge. Bring me its [core].

dialogue.hail: Heretics tried to steal the eternal flame, {name}. It burned them, and still they walk: the [fallen] priests of the south-west.
dialogue.fallen: Bring me four of their [charms], every time.
dialogue.charms: Four heretic's charms. The first time, a penitent's sash.
dialogue.caldris: Caldris the Unburnt carries a stolen ember. Bring me the [ember].

dialogue.hail: Supplies for the pilgrim road, {name}. Press G.
The flame watches us, {name}.
Smokewood never stops burning, {name}, and never burns down. The [treants] see to that.
dialogue.treants: Walking trees with ember hearts. Bring me four pieces of their [heartwood], every time.
dialogue.heartwood: Four pieces of ember heartwood. The first time, a shield of it.
dialogue.emberheart: Old Emberheart, the oldest of them. Bring me his [heart].

dialogue.hail: The beasts here are made of smoke, {name}. They bleed ash. The [smoke] wolves are the worst.
dialogue.smoke: Wolves, bears and stags of smoke. Bring me four smoke [pelts], every time.
dialogue.pelts: Four smoke pelts. The first time, gloves.
dialogue.stag: The Ashen Stag, white as bone. Bring me its [antler].

dialogue.hail: The charcoal-burners went mad in the smoke, {name}. Now they wear [masks] and worship it.
dialogue.masks: The Sootmask cult. Bring me four [fragments] of their masks, every time.
dialogue.fragments: Four soot-mask fragments. The first time, a hood.
dialogue.kolt: Their chieftain, Kolt Soot-Mask, wears antlers. Bring me his antlered [mask].

dialogue.hail: Fire [moths] the size of eagles, {name}, and mushrooms that walk. Smokewood is a strange place.
dialogue.moths: Bring me four pinches of fire moth [dust], every time.
dialogue.dust: Four pinches of fire moth dust. The first time, a cloak of moth wings.
dialogue.queen: The Cinder Moth Queen. Bring me one of her [wings].

dialogue.hail: Charcoal, bread, arrows, {name}. Press G.
Mind the smoke, {name}.
Listen, {name}. Hear that hum? The stones of Stonesail sing when the wind blows, and the [singers] sing back.
dialogue.unknown: Ask the others at the watch.
dialogue.singers: A cult that worships the stones' song. Bring me four chips of singing [stone], every time.
dialogue.stone: Four singing stone chips. The first time, a torque.
dialogue.cantor: Cantor Orla leads their choir in the north circle. Bring me her [tuning] stone.

dialogue.hail: Moor [wolves] in the heather, {name}, and wyverns on the crags. Keep your eyes up and down at once.
dialogue.wolves: Wolves and wyverns both. Bring me four moor [hides], every time.
dialogue.hides: Four moor beast hides. The first time, a cloak.
dialogue.skathe: Skathe, the great wyrm of the north-west crags. Bring me her barbed [tail].

dialogue.hail: Some of the stones out there [walk], {name}. The runes woke them, and nobody knows how to put them back to sleep.
dialogue.walk: Animated menhirs, round the great circle. Bring me four rune [shards], every time.
dialogue.shards: Four rune shards. The first time, a ring cut from one.
dialogue.thrum: Old Thrum, the oldest and loudest of them. Bring me his [heartstone].

dialogue.hail: The bog in the south-west belongs to the [hags], {name}. I'd know; I nearly joined them.
dialogue.hags: Bring me four of their hair-[knots], every time. Don't ask what I do with them.
dialogue.knots: Four hag's hair-knots. The first time, a charm.
dialogue.granny: Granny Mirewhistle, the eldest. Bring me her [ladle].

dialogue.hail: Supplies for the moor, {name}. Press G.
Mind the heather, {name}; it hides things.
Look up, {name}. The land hangs in the sky here, torn loose when Vayuketh breathed too hard. The [tempests] never settle.
dialogue.tempests: Tempest elementals, round the rift. Bring me four tempest [motes], every time.
dialogue.motes: Four tempest motes. The first time, a bracer.
dialogue.hollow: The Hollow Wind, the storm at the heart of the rift. Bring me its [eye].

dialogue.hail: Sky [serpents], {name}. They swim the air like eels swim a river, and they bite like it too.
dialogue.serpents: Bring me four serpent [plumes], every time.
dialogue.plumes: Four sky serpent plumes. The first time, a belt of them.
dialogue.coilcloud: Coilcloud, the great one of the east. Bring me her [fang].

dialogue.hail: The cloud [giants] built their hall on the highest isle, {name}, and they come down only to take.
dialogue.giants: Bring me four [cloudstones] from them, every time.
dialogue.cloudstones: Four cloudstones. The first time, vambraces.
dialogue.hauvar: Cloudlord Hauvar wears a crown of mist. Bring me the [crown].

dialogue.hail: I sailed with the sky [pirates] once, {name}. Kites, rope-lines and a wrecked skyship. I got out. Help me finish them.
dialogue.pirates: Bring me four scraps of skyship [sailcloth], every time.
dialogue.sailcloth: Four scraps of skyship sailcloth. The first time, gloves.
dialogue.mirela: Captain Mirela Driftwind. Bring me her [spyglass].

dialogue.hail: Supplies, {name}. Press G.
Keep your feet, {name}.
This is the Step, {name}: Vayuketh's stair to his summit. Storm [titans] walk the upper terraces now.
dialogue.unknown: Ask the others at the foot.
dialogue.titans: Bring me four titan's [thunderstones], every time.
dialogue.thunderstones: Four titan's thunderstones. The first time, a girdle.
dialogue.vorlaug: Vorlaug the Thunder-Titan leads them. Bring me his thunder-[torc].

dialogue.hail: The temple [guardians] were made to keep the stair, {name}. Since the Breath fell, they keep it from everyone.
dialogue.guardians: Bring me four plates of temple [bronze], every time.
dialogue.bronze: Four plates of temple bronze. The first time, boots of it.
dialogue.first: The First Guardian stands at the top of the stair. Bring me its [seal].

dialogue.hail: Thunder [drakes] nest on the terrace ledges, {name}. They ride the lightning down.
dialogue.stormscales: Four stormscales. The first time, leggings.
dialogue.thunderwing: Thunderwing, the elder drake. Bring me its [stormheart].

dialogue.hail: Vayuketh's avatar walked the summit once, {name}. Now it has [fallen]: a breath of the god gone cold and cruel.
dialogue.fallen: Its zephyrs have fallen with it. Bring me four shards of broken [breath], every time.
dialogue.breath: Four shards of broken breath. The first time, a ring.
dialogue.avatar: The Fallen Breath itself, in the temple at the top. Bring me its last [sigh], and let it rest.
dialogue.sigh: The Fallen Breath's last sigh, {name}. Vayuketh thanks you.

dialogue.hail: Supplies for the climb, {name}. Press G.
The stair is long, {name}. Pace yourself.

hunt_shouts: Not at the foot of the stair!

dialogue.hail: This was Ysmoor, {name}, a kingdom, until the fog came up out of the ground and swallowed it. Its [court] never left.
dialogue.unknown: Ask the others at the Lanternwatch.
dialogue.court: Courtiers and knights, bound in the fog. Bring me four pieces of their tarnished [silver], every time.
dialogue.silver: Four pieces of tarnished court silver. The first time, a signet.
dialogue.ismay: Queen Ismay still mourns in her throne hall. Bring me her mourning [veil], and let her rest.

dialogue.hail: Ysmoor's masons carved [gargoyles] to guard the walls, {name}. The fog woke them.
dialogue.gargoyles: Bring me four gargoyle [stones], every time.
dialogue.stones: Four gargoyle stones. The first time, vambraces of their hide.
dialogue.grimwatch: Grimwatch, the last of the great ones, on the north tower. Bring me its stone [heart].

dialogue.hail: The royal kennels ran wild in the fog, {name}. Now there are [hounds] out there white as the fog itself.
dialogue.hounds: Bring me four fog-hound [pelts], every time.
dialogue.pelts: Four fog-hound pelts. The first time, a cloak.
dialogue.whitemaw: Old Whitemaw leads the pack. Bring me his [collar]; it still bears the royal crest.

dialogue.hail: Where there are tombs there are [robbers], {name}, and Ysmoor has more tombs than living.
dialogue.robbers: Bring me back four bundles of stolen grave-[goods], every time.
dialogue.goods: Four bundles of stolen grave-goods. The first time, a sash.
dialogue.crowe: Silas Crowe, the Tomb-Taker, carries a black lantern. Bring me the [lantern].

dialogue.hail: Supplies, {name}. Press G.
Keep to the lanterns, {name}.
The great beasts came here to die for ten thousand years, {name}. Now their bones [walk].
dialogue.walk: Ivory colossi, built of a hundred skeletons. Bring me four ivory [shards], every time.
dialogue.shards: Four ivory shards. The first time, a bracer.
dialogue.ossuary: The Walking Ossuary, the greatest of them. Bring me its [heartbone].

dialogue.hail: [Poachers], {name}. They saw tusks from the dead and sell them in the south. It's a desecration.
dialogue.poachers: Bring me four pieces of poached [ivory], every time, and I'll see it laid back.
dialogue.ivory: Four pieces of poached ivory. The first time, gloves.
dialogue.varga: Tuskmonger Varga runs their camp. Bring me her tusk-[saw].

dialogue.hail: Vultures and jackals, {name}: the [carrion] eaters grow fat and bold here.
dialogue.carrion: Bring me four carrion [feathers], every time.
dialogue.feathers: Four carrion feathers. The first time, a mantle.
dialogue.gorgemaw: Gorgemaw, the carrion king, a vulture the size of a cart. Bring me its [beak].

dialogue.hail: The spirits of the great [herds] can't rest, {name}, not with poachers in their bones.
dialogue.herds: Free them. Bring me four pieces of [ghost-ivory], every time.
dialogue.grandmother: The Grandmother of Herds leads them still. Bring me her [tusk], and she'll rest.
dialogue.ghost-ivory: Four pieces of ghost-ivory. The first time, a ring.

dialogue.hail: Supplies, {name}. Press G.
Walk softly among the bones, {name}.
The sun never rises in the Unlit, {name}. Timiraj keeps it so. But the [shades] are no gift of his.
dialogue.unknown: Ask the others at the Lampward.
dialogue.shades: Bring me four shade [essences], every time.
dialogue.essences: Four shade essences. The first time, gloves of shade-silk.
dialogue.nameless: The Nameless Shade: no one remembers who it was. Bring me its [echo].

dialogue.hail: Night-[stalkers], {name}: cats of the dark with starlight in their eyes.
dialogue.stalkers: Bring me four pieces of [shadowhide], every time.
dialogue.shadowhide: Four pieces of shadowhide. The first time, boots.
dialogue.starveil: Starveil, the eldest of them. Bring me her [eye].

dialogue.hail: Giant moon [moths], {name}, drawn to anything that shines. Like us.
dialogue.moths: Bring me four pinches of luminous [dust], every time.
dialogue.dust: Four pinches of luminous dust. The first time, a sash.
dialogue.great: The Great Moon Moth. Bring me its [antenna].

dialogue.hail: House [Morvaine] fled into the endless night to feed where no sun could find them, {name}.
dialogue.morvaine: Bring me four Morvaine [crests], every time.
dialogue.crests: Four Morvaine crests. The first time, their own signet.
dialogue.countess: Countess Seraphine Morvaine, in her manor. Bring me her [locket].

dialogue.hail: Candles, lamp oil, bread, {name}. Press G.
Stay in the lamplight, {name}.

umbral_priest_casimir.name: Umbral-Priest Casimir

dialogue.hail: Welcome to Barrowhold, {name}, under the black sun. This is the shrine of [Timiraj]; I can [bind] your soul to it.
dialogue.timiraj: The Unlit. He holds the dark that lets the stars shine and the dead sleep. His followers may ask for his [blessing] once an hour.
dialogue.bind: Be still, {name}. There: the Unlit will bring you home to Barrowhold.
dialogue.unknown: Ask the guildmasters round the square.

umbral_priest_casimir.title: Keeper of the Shrine of the Unlit

blesses.refuse: The dark shelters everyone, {name}, but Timiraj's veil is for his own.
blesses.wait: You've worn his veil within the hour, {name}.
blesses.give: Close your eyes, {name}. ...Now you see as he does.

dialogue.hail: The dark doesn't frighten a warrior, {name}. Mine? Then stand in it.
dialogue.unknown: Ask Umbral-Priest Casimir at the shrine.

guildmaster.refuse: Not my trade, {name}. The others are round the square.

dialogue.hail: Even under the black sun there is light to give, {name}. Cleric?
dialogue.unknown: Ask Umbral-Priest Casimir at the shrine.

guildmaster.refuse: Not my trade, {name}. The others are round the square.

dialogue.hail: Every star is a spell, {name}, if you can read it. Wizard?
dialogue.unknown: Ask Umbral-Priest Casimir at the shrine.

guildmaster.refuse: Not my trade, {name}. The others are round the square.

dialogue.hail: Barrowhold is all shadow, {name}. A rogue's city. One of mine?
dialogue.unknown: Ask Umbral-Priest Casimir at the shrine.

guildmaster.refuse: Not my trade, {name}. The others are round the square.

dialogue.hail: The stars answer a magician's call, {name}. Shall we call them?
dialogue.unknown: Ask Umbral-Priest Casimir at the shrine.

guildmaster.refuse: Not my trade, {name}. The others are round the square.

dialogue.hail: Here the dead are honored, {name}, and they answer us. Necromancer?
dialogue.unknown: Ask Umbral-Priest Casimir at the shrine.

guildmaster.refuse: Not my trade, {name}. The others are round the square.

dialogue.hail: The ancestors are close in the dark, {name}. Shaman? Sit.
dialogue.unknown: Ask Umbral-Priest Casimir at the shrine.

guildmaster.refuse: Not my trade, {name}. The others are round the square.

dialogue.hail: Hunting in the endless night is the finest there is, {name}. Ranger?
dialogue.unknown: Ask Umbral-Priest Casimir at the shrine.

guildmaster.refuse: Not my trade, {name}. The others are round the square.

dialogue.hail: The vault keeps accounts with every bank in the land, {name}.
Supplies for every trade, {name}. Press G.
Eclipsed plate, umbral leather, starweave for the casters. Press G.
Blades forged under the black sun, {name}. Press G.
Welcome to Barrowhold, {name}. Mind the dark.
Here the gods went to war, {name}, long before any of us. What fell here never stopped [fighting].
dialogue.unknown: Ask the others at the Vigil.
dialogue.fighting: Godwar revenants, soldiers of the gods' old armies. Bring me four godwar [insignia], every time. Their [marshal] leads them still.
dialogue.insignia: Four godwar insignia. The first time, vambraces.
dialogue.marshal: The Last Marshal still calls the charge. Bring me his broken [standard].

dialogue.hail: The giants you see were [warriors] once, {name}, turned to stone mid-blow by the war's last spell. Some still move.
dialogue.warriors: Petrified warriors. Bring me four petrified [shards], every time. The mightiest of them is the [champion].
dialogue.shards: Four petrified shards. The first time, a girdle.
dialogue.champion: The Unmoving Champion. Bring me its stone [crest].

dialogue.hail: The gods built [constructs] of bronze and light to fight for them, {name}. Nobody ever told them to stop.
dialogue.constructs: Bring me four pieces of divine [bronze], every time. The great [engine] still stands among them.
dialogue.bronze: Four pieces of divine bronze. The first time, a ring.
dialogue.engine: The Godforged Engine. Bring me its [core].

dialogue.hail: [Scavengers] pick the battlefield for the gods' relics, {name}, and some of them have started eating the power inside.
dialogue.scavengers: Bring me back four stolen [relics], every time. Their [hierarch] eats the most.
dialogue.relics: Four stolen relics. The first time, gloves.
dialogue.hierarch: Hierarch Oszkar the Relic-Eater wears a crown of them. Bring me that [crown].

dialogue.hail: Supplies, {name}. Press G.
Walk softly among the fallen gods' dead, {name}.
This is Timiraj's Table, {name}, where the Unlit feasts the [honored] dead. The living were never meant to sit here.
dialogue.unknown: Ask the others at the Guest-Gate.
dialogue.honored: The honored dead guard the feast from the living. Bring me four grave-[gold] coins, every time. Their [lord] sits at the head.
dialogue.gold: Four grave-gold coins. The first time, a signet.
dialogue.lord: The Lord of the Long Table. Bring me his [goblet].

dialogue.hail: Up here the stars are close enough to fall, {name}, and the star-[giants] throw them.
dialogue.giants: Bring me four star [fragments], every time. The greatest of them is [Astrael].
dialogue.fragments: Four star fragments. The first time, boots.
dialogue.astrael: Astrael the Star-Giant. Bring me its star-[heart].

dialogue.hail: Timiraj's [hounds] run the Table, {name}. They answer only to him, and he has been silent.
dialogue.hounds: Bring me four pieces of [shadowfur], every time. The pack follows [Nightjaw].
dialogue.shadowfur: Four pieces of shadowfur. The first time, a cloak.
dialogue.nightjaw: Nightjaw, first of his hounds. Bring me its [fang].

dialogue.hail: Someone sits in Timiraj's own chair at the head of the Table, {name}: an [uninvited] guest, a dead king who would not stay dead.
dialogue.uninvited: Morcant the Uninvited, and his court of the unwelcome. Bring me four blackened [offerings] from his court, every time. And when you are ready, with friends at your side, bring me his [crown].
dialogue.offerings: Four blackened offerings. The first time, a sash.
dialogue.crown: Morcant's crown, {name}. He is no common foe; don't go alone. When the chair is empty, Timiraj will feast again.

dialogue.hail: Supplies, {name}. Press G.
Mind your manners at the god's table, {name}.

You found the way here, {name}, and the light found you on the way. I am Prabhagaj, the Dawn-Tusk. I stood at the edge of the first morning and watched the world decide to be seen. Rest by the [water]. Everything here is looked at by me, and none of it minds.
dialogue.water: Jalendra's. She let me put the morning on it. She lets very few things touch it, so I am careful with the light.
dialogue.grove: This is where the five of us stand when the world does not need us standing somewhere else. It is a [circle] for a reason: none of us is first.
dialogue.circle: Five places around the water. Mine faces the way you came in, so the first thing anyone sees here is the light. The others would tell you that was my idea. It was.
dialogue.unknown: Say it again, slower. I see well; I listen less well than I should.

dialogue.hail: Morning, {name}. It is always morning here; you'll stop noticing. I carry Prabhagaj's word when he's busy looking at something, which is always.
dialogue.unknown: Ask the god, {name}. I only carry the words.

dialogue.hail: Breathe, {name}. No, deeper. There. That was me, going in and coming out again. I am Vayuketh, He Who Breathes the Plains. I never stay anywhere long, but I always come back to the [grass] by this water.
dialogue.grass: It bends when I exhale. That is not obedience; it is agreement. Remember the difference.
dialogue.grove: The one place I stop. Do not tell the others it is my favorite. They each think it is theirs.
dialogue.unknown: Gone past me on the wind, that one. Try again.

dialogue.hail: You made it, {name}! I carry his messages. He never gives them to me here, of course; he gives them to me halfway across the world and expects me to be quick.
dialogue.unknown: Ask the god, {name}. I only carry the words.

dialogue.hail: {name}. I have your name already; I keep every one. I am Timiraj, the Unlit. The others stand in the morning here. I stand where it has not reached yet. Do not be afraid of the [dark]. It is only where you rest.
dialogue.dark: Every elephant comes to me at the end. I remember each of them. That is not the comfort it sounds like, but it is not nothing.
dialogue.grove: Even here the morning never quite arrives at my side of the water. That is how I like it, and the Dawn-Tusk has stopped trying.
dialogue.unknown: Silence answers most things better. It answers that one too.

dialogue.hail: Quietly, {name}. I write down the names he remembers, so he does not have to carry every one alone. Yours is in the book already. Everyone's is.
dialogue.unknown: Ask the god, {name}. I only carry the words.

dialogue.hail: The water made room for you before you arrived, {name}. That is my welcome; I do not give another. I am Jalendra, the Tide-Trunked. The [pond] is mine, and the rain that feeds it, and every river that leaves here for the world.
dialogue.pond: Look into it. Not at your face; past it. Every river in the world starts here as a thought. Most of them do not know it.
dialogue.grove: We come here to be still. It is harder for some of us than others. Vayuketh has never stood still in his life.
dialogue.unknown: The water does not answer that. Neither will I.

dialogue.hail: Softly, {name}. She hears everything the water touches, and the water here touches everything. I sing to it so she knows who is coming.
dialogue.unknown: Ask the god, {name}. I only carry the words.

dialogue.hail: Stand closer, {name}. Warmth is wasted on the cautious. I am Agnavar, the Ember-Tusked. Every [flame] that refused to go out has had my name in it, whether the one tending it knew or not.
dialogue.flame: The forge in Forgehold. The hearth in Emberhold. A campfire in the rain that a tired traveler would not let die. Mine, all of them. I keep count.
dialogue.grove: The others like the morning here. I like that it never becomes day. Nothing here ever finishes burning.
dialogue.unknown: Mm. Speak up. The fire is loud.

dialogue.hail: Warm yourself, {name}. I keep the embers on his dais fed. He'd do it himself, but a god tending his own fire looks like vanity.
dialogue.unknown: Ask the god, {name}. I only carry the words.

dialogue.hail: Welcome to the Grove, {name}. Mind the water; it's older than the gods standing round it. I keep the path and the arch. The gods come to the [circle] when they're ready to meet you, and when you want to go, say [return] and I'll walk you back the way you came.
dialogue.circle: Five daises round the pond, one for each of them. Some stand empty for a traveler until they've earned the god who stands there. It is not a slight; it's an invitation.
dialogue.unknown: I'm only the keeper, {name}. The gods know more than I do, and say less.

dialogue.hail: Welcome, {name}. I keep the rolls of the guilds of Emberhold. If you've a company worth naming, I can write you a [charter].
dialogue.charter: Ten platinum, and you'll need to have made level 10: a guild wants a founder who's seen something of the world. Stand here and say /guildcreate <name>, and it's yours.
dialogue.guild: A guild is a name, a roster and a voice: its members hear each other anywhere with /gu. Its leader and officers invite and remove, and set the message of the day. Ask me for a [charter].
dialogue.unknown: Charters and rolls, {name}. That's all I know.

dialogue.hail: Be still, {name}. The black water is listening. I keep the Deep-Jawed's idol, and I can [bind] your soul to Murkhold, so the bog takes you back when the world spits you out. Followers of Makarosh may ask for his [blessing].
dialogue.bind: Down on your knees in the mud, {name}. ...There. Makarosh has your scent now: you'll wake in Murkhold.
dialogue.unknown: The water doesn't answer that. Neither do I.

blesses.refuse: His blessing is for his own, {name}. The water doesn't feed strangers.
blesses.wait: You had his blessing within the hour. Patience, {name}. He has more of it than you.
blesses.give: Hold still... The deep takes a breath, and gives it to you.

dialogue.hail: HRAH. Welcome to the churned ground, {name}. I speak for the Mud-Horned. Followers of Mahishra can ask me for his [blessing]; anyone can ask me to [bind] them to Murkhold.
dialogue.bind: Stand firm. Firmer. ...Good. Mahishra's mud remembers your feet now.
dialogue.unknown: Brugg does not know. Brugg does not mind.

blesses.refuse: The Mud-Horned lends his strength to his own herd, {name}. Not to you.
blesses.wait: Once an hour. The herd doesn't stampede twice before breakfast.
blesses.give: Lower your head. ...Feel that? That's the herd behind you.

dialogue.hail: You want to hit things harder, {name}? Good. Hit them first, hit them twice, and don't stop until they're mud. I train Murkhold's warriors.
dialogue.unknown: Ask the priests. I hit things.

guildmaster.refuse: Not a fighter, {name}? Then go find someone who teaches what you are.

dialogue.hail: The spirits of the bog are hungry and patient, {name}, like everything that lives here. If you hear them, I can teach you to answer.

guildmaster.refuse: The spirits don't talk to you, {name}. I can't change that.

dialogue.hail: Mulg keeps your things. Mulg does not eat your things. Mostly. Press G.
Oolg writes the names of the warbands, {name}. Want a [charter]?
dialogue.charter: Ten platinum, and level 10 at least. Stand here and say /guildcreate <name>. Oolg will write it big.
dialogue.guild: A warband with a name, and the others hear each other with /gu. Ask Oolg for a [charter].

dialogue.hail: Flour, salt, thread, bait... all the things that aren't food yet, {name}. Press G.
Hides, straps, sacks. Everything a new bog-runner needs, {name}. And if you've got legs and patience, I could use help with a proper [pack].
dialogue.pack: A Bogtanner's pack, like the old hunters carried: toad skin, sewn tight, a shell clasp. Bring me four wallow toad skins from the pools east of the gate and I'll start on it.
dialogue.unknown: Ask Sleesh. Sleesh knows everything and sells half of it.

dialogue.hail: Iron and more iron, {name}. Some of it even has an edge. Press G.
dialogue.unknown: Thuk makes weapons. Thuk doesn't make conversation.

dialogue.hail: Keep walking, {name}. Murkhold doesn't care for strangers and cares less for trouble.
Keep walking, {name}. Murkhold doesn't care for strangers and cares less for trouble.
Quiet, {name}. You'll scare off dinner. The Wallow feeds Murkhold: rats, toads, leeches, and the frog-things to the north-east who think it's theirs. Help me keep the [pondkin] off our pools.
dialogue.pondkin: Frog-folk. They raid our traps and call it hunting. Bring me four of their beads and I'll pay, every time. And their chief, [Wetbelly], wears a crown of reeds I'd like on my wall.
dialogue.wetbelly: Fat old thing, sits in the middle of their huts to the north-east and croaks orders. Bring me his crown.
dialogue.gulpmaw: The biggest toad in the Wallow. Swallowed my brother's dog. Bring me its tongue and I'll have something made for you.
dialogue.unknown: Ask Gorra in the city. Or the priests. Not me.

dialogue.hail: Keep to the shadows, {name}. The Emberhold [scouts] camp in the east of the wood, spying on the cave. Every badge you take from them is one less pair of eyes.
dialogue.scouts: Humans from the Hearth. Four of their badges, and Duskhold pays, every time. Their captain, [Aldren], carries orders I want to read.
dialogue.aldren: Scout-Captain Aldren. He never leaves their outpost. Bring me his orders.
dialogue.silkmother: The great spider in the west of the wood. Her fang is worth a great deal to the right alchemist.

dialogue.hail: The wood is kind to those who know it, {name}, and cruel to the rest. Dresna in the city sent you about the [satchel]?
dialogue.satchel: Bring Dresna's silk to me, with two gloomfang pelts, and I'll make the body of it.
dialogue.dresna: Dresna weaves in Duskhold. If she sent silk, give it here.
dialogue.unknown: The trees don't say, and neither do I.

dialogue.hail: The Unlit remembers you, {name}, as he remembers everyone. Here, under the world, we remember him back. I can [bind] your soul to his shrine, and his followers may ask for his [blessing].
dialogue.bind: Close your eyes. It's no darker than it is with them open. ...There. You'll wake here, in his dark.

blesses.refuse: His veil is for his own, {name}.
blesses.wait: Within the hour, {name}. Even the dark keeps time.

dialogue.hail: Steel is honest, {name}. Everything else down here lies.

guildmaster.refuse: Not my art, {name}. Look elsewhere.

dialogue.hail: The Unlit gives mercy only to his own, {name}, and so do I. If you're mine, kneel.

guildmaster.refuse: Not my art, {name}. Look elsewhere.

dialogue.hail: You didn't hear me coming. Good. Neither will they, once I've finished with you.

guildmaster.refuse: Not my art, {name}. Look elsewhere.

dialogue.hail: Fire burns brighter in the dark, {name}. Let me show you how bright.

guildmaster.refuse: Not my art, {name}. Look elsewhere.

dialogue.hail: What you call, you command, {name}. What you command, you keep.

guildmaster.refuse: Not my art, {name}. Look elsewhere.

dialogue.hail: The dead are patient servants, {name}. Learn to be a patient master.

guildmaster.refuse: Not my art, {name}. Look elsewhere.

dialogue.hail: Your treasures are safe beneath the world, {name}. Safer than you are. Press G.
The houses of Duskhold are written in my book, {name}. Would you found one? Ask for a [charter].
dialogue.charter: Ten platinum, and you must have reached level 10. Stand before me and say /guildcreate <name>.
dialogue.guild: A house: a name, a roster, and a voice its members hear anywhere with /gu. Ask for a [charter].
dialogue.unknown: I keep the book of houses.

dialogue.hail: Salt, thread, flour and the rest, {name}, carried down the long stair at great expense. Press G.
Silk and leather for those who go up into the wood, {name}. And if you'll gather for me, I'll weave you a proper [satchel].
dialogue.satchel: A silkweave satchel, the kind the wood-runners carry. Start me with four strands of Duskwood spider silk; the little spiders in the wood above make it.

dialogue.hail: Dark steel, forged at the heat of the deep vents. Press G, {name}.
Keep walking, {name}. Duskhold doesn't care for strangers and cares less for trouble.
Keep walking, {name}. Duskhold doesn't care for strangers and cares less for trouble.
Murkhold and Duskhold both hunt the Rotfen, {name}, and neither trusts the other. I don't care, as long as the [lizardfolk] stop taking my traps.
dialogue.lizardfolk: The Mirescale, west of here. Four of their scales and I pay, every time. Their chief, [Sisska], carries a totem I want burned.
dialogue.sisska: Chief Sisska. Biggest lizard in the camp to the west. Bring me the totem.
dialogue.mudjaw: Old Mudjaw. A crocodile older than Murkhold, in the deep pool south-west. Bring me one of its teeth, if you can pull one.
dialogue.unknown: Ask Nyssa. She pretends to know everything.

dialogue.hail: Grisk hunts lizards. I hunt [hags]. The coven in the south-east steals our dead for their pots.
dialogue.hags: The Gristle Coven. Bring me three of their bone charms and I'll pay each time. Their mother, [Gristlewort], I want dead.
dialogue.gristlewort: Mother Gristlewort. She stirs the big cauldron in the coven's camp. Bring me her heart.
dialogue.unknown: Grisk might know. He won't tell you, but he might know.

dialogue.hail: Every thread ends somewhere, {name}. Tantuvi knows where yours does, and she isn't telling. I keep her idol; I can [bind] you to Duskhold, and her followers may ask for her [blessing].
dialogue.bind: Hold still, as the fly does. ...There. Your thread is tied here now.

blesses.refuse: Her silk is for her own, {name}.
blesses.wait: Within the hour, {name}. A web takes time to spin.
blesses.give: Be still. ...Feel the threads? They're yours for a while.

dialogue.hail: Mind the candles, {name}. Every one is a prayer, and every one is bait. I tend the Lamp-Eater's idol; I can [bind] you here, and her followers may ask for her [blessing].
dialogue.bind: Close your eyes. The light goes out, and... there. You'll wake by these candles.
dialogue.unknown: Ask the flame. It won't last long enough to answer.

blesses.refuse: The light she gives is for her own, {name}.
blesses.wait: Within the hour, {name}. Even she must wait for the next flame.
blesses.give: Breathe in. ...The candle's light is in you now.

dialogue.hail: Welcome to the March, {name}, whoever sent you. Rainhold keeps this post for anyone who'll keep the peace: bog folk, cave folk, city folk. Our trouble is [wolves], [highwaymen] and the wyvern [Scythewing].
dialogue.wolves: The march wolves run the heath in packs. Four pelts and I'll pay you, every time you bring them.
dialogue.highwaymen: The Marchreavers. They camp in the south-west and rob everyone who crosses. Three of their tokens and I pay. Their leader, [Corvel], I want answered for.
dialogue.corvel: Redhand Corvel. He wears a signet he cut off a Rainhold magistrate's finger. Bring it back to me.
dialogue.scythewing: The great wyvern of the north-east crags. Bring me a talon and I'll see you're paid for the fright.
dialogue.unknown: Ask Ossa about the dead. I only deal with the living.

dialogue.hail: Both sides buried their dead in this ground, {name}, and neither buried them deep enough. The old keep in the north-west is full of the [restless].
dialogue.restless: Soldiers of a war nobody remembers the reason for. Their armor rots, but the grave-iron in it doesn't. Three shards and I'll pay. Their [Marshal] rises at night.
dialogue.marshal: The Hollow Marshal. He walks the keep after dark and still carries his seal of command. Bring it to me and the rest may finally lie down.
dialogue.unknown: Ask the Marchwarden. He loves to talk.

dialogue.hail: Food, thread, arrows and a draught to get you home, {name}. Press G.
Mind the edge, {name}. The Cutwatch keeps the gorge road open for Rainhold, and it isn't easy. The [trolls] want the river, the [griffons] want everything else.
dialogue.trolls: The Stonefist trolls on the west bank. Three of their tusks and I'll pay, as often as you bring them. Their chief, [Grukk], wears a knuckle-bone for a charm; bring me that.
dialogue.grukk: Chief Grukk Stonefist. The biggest troll in the camp across the river.
dialogue.griffons: They nest on the crags to the north-east and take our goats and our scouts. Four feathers and I pay. The great one is [Stormcrest].
dialogue.stormcrest: A griffon as big as a boat, crest like a storm cloud. Bring me that crest plume.
dialogue.unknown: Ask Lirien. She talks to the water.

dialogue.hail: Jalendra's water falls three times into this gorge, {name}, and something has woken in it. The [spirits] of the falls are angry.
dialogue.spirits: Water spirits, risen from the falls. Their essence is holy to Jalendra; bring me three and I'll pay each time. What woke them is the [Voice].
dialogue.voice: The Voice of the Falls, at the great cascade in the south. Bring me its heart and the water will be still again.
dialogue.unknown: The water knows. I only listen.

dialogue.hail: The Northwatch, {name}: as far up the vale as the Patrol keeps a fire. Harlan's work and the hermit's, you can hand in here; I'll see it gets to them. And there's the [shrine].
dialogue.shrine: North-east, a shrine to the Dawn-Tusk nobody's prayed at since the Watch fell. There are acolytes there again, dead ones, telling [beads]. The one who leads them is [Brother Vesk].
dialogue.beads: Their prayer beads. Four, and the Patrol pays, as often as you bring them. Every bead you take is one less prayer to whatever they pray to now.
dialogue.brother vesk: He kept that shrine when the Watch still stood. Now he keeps it for something else. His censer still smokes: bring it to me.
dialogue.unknown: Ask Harlan, back down the road. He's walked it longer.

dialogue.hail: Food, water and arrows, {name}, and not a coin more than it cost to haul them out here. Press G.
dialogue.unknown: Ask the scout. I only count the stores.

dialogue.hail: The road's watched from here, {name}. Anything chasing you, bring it past me.
The road's watched from here, {name}. Anything chasing you, bring it past me.
The road's watched from here, {name}. Anything chasing you, bring it past me.
The road's watched from here, {name}. Anything chasing you, bring it past me.
Don't mind the mess, {name}. We had a camp here, six of us, until [Old Greyback] came. And the [boars] that follow him about for his leavings.
dialogue.boars: Tuskers, the size of a cart. Four of their tusks and I'll pay, again and again: I'm selling them to the Patrol for spear points.
dialogue.old greyback: A bear, grey as ash, with a scar down his back where my brother's axe went in. He sleeps west of the camp. Bring me his hide and we can come home.
dialogue.unknown: I cut wood, {name}. Ask the hermit.

dialogue.hail: Windrider's Rest, {name}: Galehold's last fire before the herds. Whatever the city's asked of you out here, you can hand in to me; the riders carry it back. Mind the [stones] up north.
dialogue.stones: A ring of standing stones in the north grass, humming. They get up and walk now, the [sentinels], and something wakes in the middle of them: the [Ringwarden].
dialogue.sentinels: Stone that walks. Bring me four chips of it and I'll pay, as often as you like: Galehold's stonecutters want to know what they're made of.
dialogue.ringwarden: The biggest of the stones, the one in the middle. It carries a rune-stone in its chest. Bring me that.
dialogue.unknown: Galehold's the place for questions. I'm the place for answers you can use.

dialogue.hail: Food, water and arrows, {name}, and not a coin more than it cost to haul them out here. Press G.
dialogue.unknown: Ask the scout. I only count the stores.

That was my husband's camp, {name}, before the fever took the herd and the Khan took the riders. Now the [jackals] have it. And [Old Rakemaw].
dialogue.jackals: Carrion jackals, come for the bones. Bring me four of their ears and I'll pay you every time: I'll have them gone from that camp if I have to buy every ear on the plain.
dialogue.old rakemaw: The pack's old mother. Grey muzzle, one eye. She dens in my husband's yurt. Bring me her jawbone.
dialogue.unknown: I only know the herd, {name}. What's left of it.

dialogue.hail: Saltwater Well, {name}: the only sweet water north of the waystation, and the caravans' last stop before the pan. Suri's and Ibrem's business you can hand in here. And ask me about the [mine].
dialogue.mine: The old salt mine east of here. The miners never left: the brine got into them. They wander the shacks still, with their [tags] round their necks, and their [foreman] with them.
dialogue.tags: Their mine tags. Bring me four and I'll pay each time; their families in Lanternhold will want to know.
dialogue.foreman: Foreman Dask. He kept the ledger. Bring it to me and the families will know who went down and didn't come up.
dialogue.unknown: Suri knows the road. I know the water.

The road's watched from here, {name}. Anything chasing you, bring it past me.
My caravan, {name}. Lost to the salt in a storm, three years ago. I came back for the cargo and found the [crabs] living in it. And the [Wreck-Shell].
dialogue.crabs: Salt crabs, big ones, nesting in the wagons. Four of their claws and I'll pay: the cooks in Lanternhold pay me more.
dialogue.wreck-shell: The old one. A shell like a wagon wheel. It lives under the lead wagon, on my strongbox. Bring me a piece of its shell and I'll know it's done.
dialogue.unknown: I trade, {name}. I don't know much else.

dialogue.hail: Cinderwatch, {name}: the Ashwatch's fire on the north road. The Warden's business, Mott's, Ilse's and the Ashseer's, you can all hand in here. And ask me about the [chapel].
dialogue.unknown: Ask back at camp. I only watch the far end.
dialogue.husks: Husks, burned in the chapel when the fire came through, still at their prayers. Four of their rosary beads and the Forge pays you, every time.
dialogue.deacon: The Kindled Deacon. He led the prayers when the chapel burned, and he's leading them still. Bring me his censer.
dialogue.chapel: South-east, a chapel that burned with its congregation inside. They're still in there: [husks], and their [deacon].

The road's watched from here, {name}. Anything chasing you, bring it past me.
Mind the rift, {name}. There's ore down there, Forge-grade, if you can get past the [newts]. And [Old Blisterback].
dialogue.newts: Cinder newts, fat with fire. Four of their blisters and I'll pay, as often as you like: the Forge uses them for flux.
dialogue.old blisterback: The biggest newt in the rift, blistered all over. Bring me the heartstone out of him.

dialogue.hail: Glasswater Camp, {name}: the traders' last fire before the glass. Rahel's work, Anouk's, Bram's, Kiri's, you can hand it all in to me. And ask me about the [skiff].
dialogue.unknown: Ask back at camp. I only watch the far end.
dialogue.salters: A skiff went down in the far north-east, crew and all, and the salt kept them. They wander still. Their lockets, four at a time, and I'll pay.
dialogue.dunmore: Skiffmaster Dunmore. He still walks his deck. Bring me his logbook.
dialogue.skiff: A sand-skiff wrecked north-east of here, on a crossing nobody finished. The [salters] still crew it, and [Dunmore] still has the helm.

The road's watched from here, {name}. Anything chasing you, bring it past me.
The pillars, {name}! Salt, grown like glass, and something wakes in them. [Sentinels]. And the [Pillarmother].
dialogue.sentinels: The sentinels grow out of the pillars and walk. Four chips of them and I'll pay, again and again.
dialogue.pillarmother: The Pillarmother. The oldest pillar, and the others grow from her. Bring me her core.

dialogue.hail: Hollowtusk Camp, {name}: Tuskwatch's fire at the crossroads. Anything the Bonewarden or the others asked of you, hand it in here. And ask me about the [gate].
dialogue.unknown: Ask back at camp. I only watch the far end.
dialogue.shades: Shades gather at the Tusk Gate, starving for the herds they drove. Four of their beads and I'll pay, every time.
dialogue.mahout: The Hollow Mahout drove the great herds here to die, and drives them still. Bring me his goad.
dialogue.gate: North-east, the Tusk Gate: an arch of tusks where the old herds came in to die. [Shades] wait there, and the [Mahout] who drove them.

Good ivory in that hollow, {name}, if the [beetles] would let a body work. And their [Marrow Queen].
dialogue.unknown: I carve, {name}. The Bonewarden knows the rest.
dialogue.beetles: Beetles that eat the marrow out of the old bones. Four of their shells and I'll pay, as often as you bring them.
dialogue.marrow queen: The Marrow Queen, as big as a cart, laying in the great ribcage. Bring me her mandible.

dialogue.hail: The Heronwatch, {name}: the Reedwatch's island out in the middle. Pallavi's work, Kesh's, the Priestess's, you can hand it in here and save the wade back. And ask me about the [bell].
dialogue.unknown: Ask back at camp. I only watch the far end.
dialogue.ringers: The bell-ringers of the north hamlet, drowned at their ropes when the water came. Four of their clappers and I'll pay, every time.
dialogue.bellwarden: The Bellwarden. He rang the flood bell too late, and now he rings it for the drowned. Bring me the bell.
dialogue.bell: North, a hamlet the marsh took, stilts and all. Its [ringers] still ring the flood bell, and the [Bellwarden] with them.

dialogue.unknown: Ask the scout. I only count the stores.

That was my weir, {name}, before the [eels] came up it. And the [Eel-Mother] behind them.
dialogue.unknown: I fish, {name}. Ask Kesh about boats.
dialogue.eels: Eels, thick as your arm, up from the deep channels. Four of their fins and I'll pay, again and again.
dialogue.eel-mother: The Eel-Mother, the one they all came up behind. Bring me her eye.

dialogue.hail: The Channelwatch, {name}: between the middle and east channels, as far up the delta as Rainhold keeps a fire. Sione's work, the Headman's, Anh's and Cato's, you can hand in here. And ask me about the [rookery].
dialogue.unknown: Ask back at camp. I only watch the far end.
dialogue.toads: Delta toads, the size of a dog, crowding the rookery rocks. Four of their glands and I'll pay, every time: the apothecaries in Rainhold want them.
dialogue.gulmog: Gulmog the Bellower, the old bull of the rookery. You'll hear him before you see him. Bring me his throat-sac.
dialogue.rookery: Far north-east, where the channels start, a rock rookery full of [toads]. And the bull, [Gulmog].
