Mind the mangroves, {name}. The roots walk here: [lurkers], and the old one they call [Tanglefoot].
dialogue.lurkers: The lurkers are the mangroves themselves, walking. Four of their roots and I'll pay you, as often as you bring them: they make the best poultice in the Monsoon.
dialogue.tanglefoot: Tanglefoot is the oldest of them. His heartroot is black as tar. Bring it to me.

dialogue.hail: Glassfire Camp, {name}: the Forge's only fire on the glass. Solveig's work, Uzma's, Farid's and Captain Ragna's, you can hand it all in here, and save the walk to Forgehold. Ask me about the [borers].
dialogue.unknown: Ask back at camp. I only watch the far end.
dialogue.borers: West, a Forge watch the glass swallowed whole, men and all. The [borers] are digging them out again, and the [Sable Borer] is the worst.
dialogue.sable borer: The Sable Borer, black as the glass it eats. It dug the watchmen out of the glass to get at them. Bring me its mandible.

You see the lights, {name}? The garden grows them. [Wisps], and something brighter at the heart: [Prism-Heart].
dialogue.unknown: I read the glass. Hrafn reads the rest.
dialogue.wisps: The wisps are light the glass caught and won't let go. Four of their prisms and I'll pay, every time.
dialogue.prism-heart: Prism-Heart, the brightest of them, at the garden's pool. Bring me its core, and the garden will go dark.

dialogue.hail: Emberfall Camp, {name}: the woodwardens' fire in the heart of the wood. Sefa's work, Bartek's, Liesl's, Ondine's, hand it in here. And ask me about the [hollow].
dialogue.unknown: Ask back at camp. I only watch the far end.
dialogue.shamblers: In the north-west hollow the fungus walks. Four of their spore sacs and I'll pay, every time: burned, they keep the moths off.
dialogue.rotcap: The Rotcap is the mother of the hollow, tall as a treant. Bring me its gills.
dialogue.hollow: North-west, a hollow where the fungus grows taller than the trees: [shamblers], and the one they grow from, the [Rotcap].

My kilns, {name}. We burned charcoal here for the Forge until the [imps] moved into them. And [Old Bellows].
dialogue.unknown: I burn wood, {name}. Vard sells what I burn.
dialogue.imps: Imps, nesting in my kilns and keeping them hot. Four of their cinders and I'll pay, again and again.
dialogue.old bellows: Old Bellows, the big one. He sleeps in the middle kiln and blows it white-hot. Bring me his horn.

dialogue.hail: The Westwatch, {name}: the Moorwatch's fire past the great circle. Aldous's work, Wenna's, Idris's and Agathe's, you can hand it in here. And ask me about the [kite hill].
dialogue.unknown: Ask back at camp. I only watch the far end.
dialogue.harriers: Harriers took the kite hill when the kite-flyers left it. Four of their flight-feathers and I'll pay, every time: Galehold fletches with them.
dialogue.talonmere: Old Talonmere, the hen of the hill. She took a kite-flyer once, kite and all. Bring me her talon.
dialogue.kite hill: North-east, where Galehold's kite-flyers used to fly. The [harriers] took it, and [Old Talonmere] rules it.

The cairns are waking, {name}. Old kings under the moor, and their [wights] with them. The oldest is the [Cairn-King].
dialogue.unknown: I read the stones. Idris cuts them.
dialogue.wights: The wights of the cairns walk at the ring. Four of their bones, and I'll lay them back, and pay you for every four.
dialogue.cairn-king: The Cairn-King. His torc is the last gold on the moor. Bring it to me, and the cairns will sleep.

dialogue.hail: The Highwatch, {name}: Driftwatch's fire under the cloud hall. Imani's work, Kael's, Benedikt's, the Bosun's, hand it in here. And ask me about the [fallen isle].
dialogue.unknown: Ask back at camp. I only watch the far end.
dialogue.rays: Cloud rays feed round the isle that fell, north-east. Four of their tail-barbs and I'll pay, every time: Galehold tips its harpoons with them.
dialogue.stormbarb: Old Stormbarb, the oldest ray over the isle, grey as a thundercloud. Bring me its spine.
dialogue.fallen isle: North-east, an isle that lost its tether and came down. The [rays] feed round it, and [Stormbarb] is the oldest of them.

My glider, {name}, or what's left of it. The [sprites] tore it down, and their [Gustmother] with them.
dialogue.unknown: I build kites, {name}. Tarrow flies them.
dialogue.sprites: The sprites weave ribbons of wind and wear them. Four of the ribbons and I'll pay, again and again: they make the best kite-tails.
dialogue.gustmother: The Gustmother is the wind the sprites come from. Catch her breath in a jar and bring it to me.

dialogue.hail: The Crossroads Lantern, {name}: as far into the fog as the Lanternwatch keeps a flame. Evander's work, Hilde's, Osric's, Cassia's, hand it in here. And ask me about the [crypt].
dialogue.unknown: Ask back at camp. I only watch the far end.
dialogue.wraiths: The crypt north-west has no lanterns left, and the wraiths walk out of it. Four scraps of their shrouds and I'll pay, every time.
dialogue.chaplain: The Veiled Chaplain buried Ysmoor's dead, and reads over them still. Bring me his psalter.
dialogue.crypt: North-west, Ysmoor's old crypt, the lanterns all out. [Wraiths] come out of it, and the [Chaplain] who kept it.

The road's watched from here, {name}. Anything chasing you, bring it past me.
Ysmoor was built from this quarry, {name}, and the stone doesn't want to be quarried any more. [Rubble] gets up and walks. And [Old Cairnback].
dialogue.unknown: I cut stone. Hilde sets it.
dialogue.rubble: Rubble that walks, in my quarry. Four chips of it and I'll pay, again and again: Hilde needs the stone.
dialogue.cairnback: Old Cairnback is the old quarry face itself, come loose. Bring me the keystone out of him.

dialogue.hail: The Midnight Lamp, {name}: the Lampward's fire in the middle of the dark. Solenne's work, Kwame's, Yuna's, Aurelio's, hand it in here. And ask me about the [folly].
dialogue.unknown: Ask back at camp. I only watch the far end.
dialogue.hounds: The Countess keeps her hounds at her summerhouse, east, behind the iron fence: Morvaine's Folly. Four of their collar-studs and I'll pay, every time.
dialogue.blackfang: Blackfang, her favorite. Bring me its collar, and she'll know who took it.
dialogue.folly: East, the Countess's summerhouse behind an iron fence: Morvaine's Folly. Her [hounds] run there, and her pet, [Blackfang].

This well held the moon, {name}, before the moon went out. Now [wisps] rise out of it, and the [Pale Keeper].
dialogue.unknown: I keep the well. Solenne keeps the lamps.
dialogue.wisps: The wisps carry the last of the moon's water. Four drops and I'll pay you, as often as you bring them.
dialogue.pale keeper: The Pale Keeper was the well's first warden. Bring me his lantern, and the well will sleep.

dialogue.hail: The Last Fire, {name}: the Vigil's camp under the Marshal's hill. Mateo's work, Freydis's, Kanoa's, Wilhelmina's, hand it in here. And ask me about the [blade].
dialogue.unknown: Ask back at camp. I only watch the far end.
dialogue.sentinels: North-east, a god's sword lies broken in the ground, and its shards stand up and guard it. Four flecks of the steel and I'll pay, every time.
dialogue.warden: The Blade's Warden guards the hilt. Bring me the gem out of it.
dialogue.blade: North-east, where a god's sword broke. Its shards stand guard: [sentinels], and the [Warden] at the hilt.

The dig's mine, {name}, if I could get at it. The war-[hounds] of the last charge are still buried here, and they don't like being dug up. [Ashfang] least of all.
dialogue.unknown: I dig. Wilhelmina keeps what I find.
dialogue.hounds: The hounds of the last charge, dug up and walking. Four of their bones and I'll pay, as often as you bring them.
dialogue.ashfang: Ashfang led the charge. Bring me the war-collar off him.

dialogue.hail: The High Shelter, {name}: the pilgrims' last rest before the monastery. Brother Tenzin's work and the Tea-Mother's, you can hand it in here. And ask me about the [stupa].
dialogue.unknown: Ask back at camp. I only watch the far end.
dialogue.pilgrims: West, a stupa pilgrims died at in the snow, before they reached the monastery. They haunt it still. Four of their prayers and I'll pay, every time.
dialogue.unshriven: The Unshriven led them. He rings his bell for a monastery that never answers. Bring it to me.
dialogue.stupa: West, a stupa where pilgrims froze on the way up. They're still there: forsaken [pilgrims], and the [Unshriven] who led them.

The road's watched from here, {name}. Anything chasing you, bring it past me.
The road's watched from here, {name}. Anything chasing you, bring it past me.
The shielings are ours in summer, {name}, but the [wolves] came down early this year. And [Old Frostjaw] with them.
dialogue.unknown: I keep yaks, {name}. The Tea-Mother keeps everything else.
dialogue.wolves: The high wolves came down to the shielings. Four pelts and I'll pay, every time: the yaks sleep easier.
dialogue.frostjaw: Old Frostjaw leads them, white as the snow. Bring me his fang.
